101	**OPEN — GH3 game-launch handoff (needs a BT sniffer):** when a game disc boots, the
102	Wii goes HID-silent toward fauxmote for many seconds, then drops the link (`rsn 0x08`).
103	A manual `reconnect` re-establishes the link, but the session isn't reliably usable in-game.
104	A real Wiimote rides the handoff with a quick ~2 s LED off/on. fauxmote's own logs
105	don't show *why* the Wii goes silent on us vs a real Wiimote — there's no command we
106	visibly mishandle (zero RX reports during the gap). Diagnosing needs a Bluetooth
107	sniffer to diff a real Wiimote vs fauxmote through the GH3 launch. **Workaround for
108	now: restart fauxmote after the game has started** (a fresh boot reconnects cleanly).
109	The recurring `mode 3 … BASIC mode` reconnect warning is likely a red herring (real
110	Wiimotes use Basic-mode L2CAP for HID). Revisit after the guitar extension — GH3 may
111	engage the controller differently once it sees a guitar.
112	
113	**Other notes:**
114	- **Keep-awake:** the Wii idle-disconnects on lack of *input*; streaming reports +
115	  occasional button activity keeps it alive (free during gameplay).
116	- **Caveat:** a Wiimote cannot power a Wii on from standby (BT radio off); "wake" only
117	  means reconnecting while the console is already running.
118	
119	Phase progression and success criteria are in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) §6.

123	## Decision log
124	
125	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
126	|------|----------|-----------|
127	| 2026-06-13 | **Removed the persistent auto-reconnect task; recovery is the manual `reconnect` command only.** Drops just reset state (`Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected`); no automatic re-initiation. | Auto-reconnect neither survived the GH3 game-launch handoff nor served as a keep-awake mechanism (reconnecting ≠ staying awake). Keeping the Wii awake is better done with occasional input/state changes, which Marvin's command stream provides during use. Removing it also drops the slot-leak/backoff complexity. The sniff-delay override (idle→sniff = 65 s) stays — that genuinely prevents idle supervision-timeout drops. |
128	| 2026-06-13 | **Extension encryption is mandatory for GH3 and implemented in the base Wiimote (`ext_crypto.c`); the guitar module stays plaintext.** GH3's real key handshake (register trace): `0x55`→`0xf0` (disable) → read ID `0xfa` in clear → `0xAA`→`0xf0` (enable) → 16-byte key to `0x40`-`0x4f`. The base captures the key, derives ft/sb, and encrypts outgoing ext data (streamed bytes @ offset `0x08`; reg reads @ `addr & 7`). | Everything GH3 reads from the extension is decrypted with that key, so plaintext is garbage (the "green/red worked unencrypted" observation was a decryption coincidence). Encryption is a generic Wiimote feature (nunchuk/classic encrypt too), so it belongs in the base, not the guitar. Corrects the plan's guess that GH3 used the old `0→0x40` init. |
129	| 2026-06-13 | **Cipher tables come from Dolphin's 1st-party set, not `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator`'s `wm_crypto.c`.** rnconrad's S-boxes are corrupted (sbox[3]@0x60, [4]@0xd8, [6]@0x88/0xec are `0xD0`/`0xF0` & `0xD2`/`0xE2` transcription flips → not valid permutations). Used Dolphin's `keygen_sbox_1st_party` + `sboxes_1st_party[8]`; verified the key-schedule/encrypt algorithm term-for-term against Dolphin and round-tripped GH3's real key (idx 0, encrypt→decrypt identity). | Wrong table bytes silently corrupt the keystream → undebuggable "notes are garbage." Dolphin is GPL and validated against real games; the marcan tables are reverse-engineered hardware constants (facts), reproduced with our own code. |
130	| 2026-06-13 | **Guitar is a self-registering extension module behind `wiimote_ext.h`; `wiimote.c` is extension-agnostic.** `wiimote_extension_t` = register bank + `build_report`/`set_button`/`reset`; `Wiimote_RegisterExtension`. Buttons drive by name via `Wiimote_SetButton`/`TapButton`. | Plans for other extensions (nunchuk/classic) as drop-in `*.c` files, keeps the base generic, and keeps the CLI as thin pass-throughs over the same API Marvin will use. |
131	| 2026-06-13 | **Byte0/1 bits 7-6 must be set (GH3 Les Paul ident); single IR calibration kept.** Clear ident bits make GH3 treat us as a GHWT guitar and ignore the strum bar. Basic-IR pointer is correct on the main Wii screen with the same calibration as extended; the GH3-internal Home-overlay mis-scaling is GH3's own transform and is moot (IR is physically blocked when the Wiimote is in the guitar — guitar-mode Home nav uses the analog stick). | Found by hardware testing. No second/basic-mode calibration: the format packing is provably identical to extended (Dolphin + Linux), so the only real difference (GH3) isn't ours to fix and doesn't matter on real hardware. |
132	| 2026-06-12 | **`esp_hidd` is a dead end for Wii emulation; the only working ESP-IDF path is a custom SDP record (internal Bluedroid `SDP_*` API) + raw L2CAP HID on PSM 0x11/0x13 (`esp_bt_l2cap`), with the hardcoded SDP buffer raised.** Two independent walls: (1) the Wii rejects esp_hidd's record even with a small descriptor (wrong HID attribute values — subclass/reconnect-initiate/etc., which esp_hidd hardcodes and doesn't expose); (2) the real 217-byte descriptor can't even be registered — `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` (the per-record attribute pad) is **hardcoded 300** (`sdp_db.c:495`, `bluedroid_user_config.h`; no menuconfig), and the full Wiimote record is ~463 B → `SDP_AddAttribute fail … ID 518`. Confirmed feasible building blocks in IDF v6.0.1: `SDP_CreateRecord`/`SDP_AddAttribute`/`SDP_AddSequence` (private `stack/sdp_api.h`) and `esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(psm)`. | Bluedroid is the only Classic-BT stack on ESP32, and its public APIs can't host an arbitrary SDP record (`esp_sdp` RAW is search-only). So the path requires *unsupported internals*: raise `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` via an injected `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN` compile define, build the exact Wiimote record with the internal SDP DB API, skip esp_hidd, and serve HID over raw L2CAP + hand-rolled HIDP. Heavy + fragile across IDF updates, but it's the real route. The exact 463-byte record + 217-byte descriptor are saved at [`wiimote-sdp.md`](wiimote-sdp.md). |
133	| 2026-06-12 | **Q1 resolved: ESP-IDF `esp_hidd`'s auto-generated SDP record is NOT accepted by the Wii → pivot to raw L2CAP (listen on PSM 0x11 control / 0x13 data) + a hand-built SDP record matching a real Wiimote.** Verbose Bluedroid logs: the Wii opens an ACL link, connects to our SDP server (PSM 1), reads our records (we send 14/250/37-byte SDP responses), then disconnects the SDP channel and terminates the ACL (`rsn 0x13` = remote user terminated) **without ever opening the HID PSMs**. SSP was confirmed off this round (legacy pairing) and discovery works (limited-discoverable + COD `0x002504`), so SDP content is the only remaining blocker. Wii BD_ADDR observed: `00:17:ab:07:2c:21`. | The Wii validates the SDP record against a real Wiimote's; esp_hidd's generic HID record (right VID/PID, wrong attributes + HID descriptor) fails the check, so it never proceeds to HID. Matches why `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator` replaces the host BT stack to serve the exact SDP. Open: whether ESP-IDF lets us serve a fully custom SDP record (esp_sdp API vs internal Bluedroid `SDP_*` API) and listen on the fixed HID PSMs via `esp_bt_l2cap`. |
134	| 2026-06-12 | **Phase 1 first attempt uses ESP-IDF's unified `esp_hidd` BT-classic HID device wearing the Wiimote identity, not a hand-rolled raw-L2CAP/SDP stack.** `bt_hid_device.c`: `esp_hidd_dev_init(ESP_HID_TRANSPORT_BT)` with VID `0x057e`/PID `0x0306`/version `0x0100`/name `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01`, COD set to `0x002504` (peripheral/joystick), a minimal vendor-defined report map (just report IDs 0x30 in / 0x12 out), **SSP disabled** (`CONFIG_BT_SSP_ENABLED=n`) for legacy PIN pairing, and a GAP `PIN_REQ` handler that replies with the requesting host's BD_ADDR reversed. | The stack already implements HIDP + L2CAP (PSM 0x11/0x13) + auth, so this is the cheapest probe of Q1: if a real Wii connects + authenticates against the auto-generated SDP, we avoid hand-building raw SDP entirely. If it rejects it, fall back to raw L2CAP + the exact SDP record from `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator` (cloned locally for byte-exact bytes; WebFetch can't reproduce the ~463-byte blob). |
135	| 2026-06-12 | **Target the console-SYNC *bonding* flow, not the 1+2 temporary flow.** PIN handler returns the connecting host's (Wii's) BD_ADDR reversed (`param->pin_req.bda` byte-reversed). | Bonding (red SYNC button under the Wii's SD cover + controller in sync mode) is how a controller gets *persistently* registered, which is what a robot wants. The 1+2 flow is one-time/temporary and uses the controller's own address instead. Resolves Q2. |
136	| 2026-06-12 | **Build fauxmote as a parallel, independent proof-of-concept subproject; the fretboard GPIO-press path stays authoritative.** New top-level firmware subproject `firmware/fauxmote/`. | Device-side Wiimote *emulation* to a real Wii is rare/novel (host-side use is common), so de-risk it in isolation before touching marvin/fretboard/edge-ai. Nothing in the existing actuation path changes until fauxmote is proven. |
137	| 2026-06-12 | **Framework = ESP-IDF (v6.x; v6.0.1 installed), Bluedroid in Bluetooth-Classic-only mode (BLE disabled).** | Wiimote uses Bluetooth Classic HID; ESP-IDF exposes the BT-Classic HID-device API (`esp_hidd_api.h`), custom SDP records, BD_ADDR control, and raw L2CAP — all of which emulation needs. Arduino-ESP32's BT-Classic HID-device support is too thin for the custom SDP/descriptor the Wiimote requires. |
138	| 2026-06-12 | **Board = Adafruit ESP32 Feather V2 (product 5400); its *original* ESP32 is the load-bearing choice.** | The original ESP32 has a Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR) radio. ESP32-S3/C3 are BLE-only and cannot emulate a Wiimote. Confirmed the product 5400 is the Feather V2 (not a QT Py S3). |
139	| 2026-06-12 | **marvin↔fauxmote command link is deferred; early phases use a local test command source.** | Lets the hard part (ESP32↔Wii Bluetooth emulation) be developed and validated standalone. The likely eventual link mirrors the fretboard 1-byte fret/strum bitmask over UART, but that's a later-session decision. |

231	  **non-blocking** — empty rx queue returns `0` (not EOF), peer-close returns `-1`
232	  (errno `EPIPE`). So poll on `0`, exit only on `<0` (first cut wrongly treated `0`
233	  as EOF and the reader exited instantly). No `select` support on this VFS.
234	- First output report from the Wii (data channel, PSM 0x13): `a2 17 00 00 17 70 00
235	  01` = report `0x17` Read Memory, EEPROM offset `0x001770`, size 1. The Wii then
236	  **blocks waiting for our `0x21` (Read Data) reply** — confirms the report
237	  responder is the gate to a live/assigned controller. → Phase 2b.

Strum recall generalises to ~the overfit ceiling (.965 vs .97). **Red is the one laggard (.890)** — not a corpus-coverage gap (slowride red density 26 % is mid-pack); flagged as open follow-up. Old pre-fix baseline for contrast: held-out frets 80–94 %, strum recall ~30 %.

23	- **Runtime weight-swap (per-difficulty) supported.** Per-model int8 params are bundled in a `model_def_t`; the emitter writes one named `model_<name>` (prefixed symbols, `--name`), arch dims are shared `#define`s with a `_Static_assert` (mismatched-arch model = build error), and `MODEL_DEFAULT` = first included. `model_infer_set_model(&model_<name>)` swaps at runtime (recomputes the need-set, keeps the ring so no re-warm). Multiple models link via an aggregator `model_weights.h` that `#include`s the per-difficulty headers. Smoke-tested: `model_hard` + `model_expert` coexist, init→hard, swap→expert, bit-exact preserved. Selection signal in standalone mode (button/serial/scroll-speed sensor) is still open (see open questions).

42	## Decision log
43	
44	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
45	|------|----------|-----------|
46	| 2026-06-04 | **Deploy model = 16 channels (not the 8ch training default), trained on the full 5-song corpus (`--no-holdout`), `--strum-weight 5`, 50 epochs; quantised at strum thresh 0.80 / refractory 8.** | 8ch is capacity-limited on the sparse strum class (proven: 8ch overfit strum recall ~.86 vs 64ch ~.99; on hardware the 8ch full-corpus model overstrummed and no threshold fixed it — 0.85 missed real strums *and* still overstrummed, i.e. the precision/recall curve itself was the wall). 16ch lifts the curve (mono .856/.969 → .942/.981) so a threshold lands both. Affordable because inference now runs in the main loop, not the ISR — ~12.5k MACs / ~2–3 ms, 240 Hz sampling unaffected, RAM ~4 KB of 8 KB. `--strum-weight 5` (< the ~8–10 auto) trims the recall bias at the source. Threshold stays a header-only knob (0.80↔0.85 the live range). |
47	| 2026-06-04 | **Corpus + firmware timing pinned at `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS=300` / `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS=40` (marvin `8e5d18`, tuned for hard).** The 5-song hard corpus was captured at these values; the model is only valid for the timing it was distilled from — do **not** mix captures from other timing regimes (e.g. the old 220/25) into one corpus. If timing changes again, re-capture the whole corpus. | The deployed model *is* the timing function (photo→fret+strum), so the strum onset it learns is set by `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS` and the pulse width by `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS`. Mixing regimes would teach two different photo→strum lags for identical inputs — the same ill-posed averaging as mixing difficulties. No model/architecture change needed for the 220→300/25→40 bump: the RF85 overfit A/B was *itself* run on this 300/40 corpus and fit it (frets 0.99, strum recall 0.97, p95 16.7 ms), which empirically proves RF85 covers this timing's lag; the monostable also normalises the output pulse to `--strum-hold`, so the wider 40 ms label pulse doesn't force a knob change. |
48	| 2026-06-04 | **Default model RF widened to `(1,4,16)` (RF 85) from `(1,4)` (RF 21).** Added a `--dilations` CLI flag; saved in the checkpoint and read back at eval (fallback `(1,4)` for pre-flag checkpoints). | Overfit A/B on clean line-263 `actuator-fb` data (slowride-hard, train==eval): RF21 caps at frets ~0.86 / loss plateau 0.31 — it can't see back to the photo cue ~48 samples before the strike line, so it can't hold the fret. RF85 (50k MACs, under the ~100k budget) recovers to frets 0.97–0.99 / strum recall 0.97 / p95 16.7 ms. Exactly the masked-by-detfb limitation model.md predicted would bite `actuator-fb`. Frets are the headline; widening RF costs ~19k MACs and is well affordable. |
49	| 2026-06-03 | **Primary path is programmatic (PyTorch), not MPLAB ML / SensiML.** MPLAB ML is demoted to an eventual *parallel demonstration* track, not the critical path. Inverts [`training.md` §5.1](training.md), which had the auto-pipeline first. | The hard part of this task is *temporal strum timing* — learning the photo-dip→strum delay over a causal window. SensiML's AutoML is feature-extraction + tree/ensemble over windowed stats: strong at "classify this window," weak at sequence/event-timing, which is exactly the part we care about (and review.md already named a causal 1D-CNN as the fallback). PyTorch gives full control over the window-length sweep (the #1 hyperparameter, [review.md Q3](review.md)), the sparse-strum class weighting, and the custom Phase-2 eval metrics (per-bit accuracy + strum-event timing distribution + visual side-by-side) the gate is judged on. Cost accepted: we own int8 quantisation + the on-device inference C in Phase 3 — tractable for a ≲1 k-MAC, 2-conv model, and the bit-exact control actually helps Phase 3's "matches host inference" gate. MPLAB ML stays valuable later as the Microchip-tooling demonstration once a known-good shape exists. |
50	| 2026-06-03 | **v1 trains on a single difficulty — Expert.** Corpus = many songs at Expert, one held out. NOT mixed-difficulty (which reverses the old [`review.md`](review.md) "train on Easy+Med+Expert" prescription). | If the game's highway scroll speed varies with difficulty, the photo-dip→strum delay = `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + 220 ms` — the first term is inversely proportional to scroll speed. With 5 sensors at one row and no difficulty input, identical inputs map to different correct delays across difficulties: an ill-posed regression the model can only resolve by averaging (wrong on all). This is an *observability* gap, not a coverage gap, so more mixed data can't fix it. Single-difficulty is low-regret: if scroll speed turns out constant we lose nothing and can merge later; if it varies we've dodged the ill-posed case. Expert chosen for densest strum signal (helps the ~5.8 % rare class) and shortest delay (smallest window). Eventual structure if speed varies: one model per difficulty, difficulty selected at runtime from marvin's game-state controller. |
51	| 2026-06-03 | Phase 1 exporter implemented as a `--labels={detector,actuator}` switch on the existing `export-ml` command rather than a new subcommand. Default stays `detector` (back-compat); `actuator` emits the `fret_*,strum` schema. | The two modes share the whole capture-read / timestamp / forward-fill loop; only the label-source record (`Detector` vs `Actuator`) and the output columns differ. A flag keeps one code path and one set of edge-case handling (missing SESSION, pre-label rows, strict mode). The detector path's CSV bytes are unchanged, so the existing corpus/tooling keeps working. |
52	| 2026-06-03 | `n_strum_events` stat counts **rising edges** (0→1 transitions) of the collapsed strum bit, not strum-active rows. | "Events" = distinct strums, which is the quantity to sanity-check against a song's note count. Per-row density ("a few %") is still eyeballable from the CSV; the rising-edge count is the more information-dense single number and doesn't conflate hold-duration with strum count. |
53	| 2026-06-03 | Collapsed strum bit computed from `Actuator.intended_mask` bits 5\|6 (the doc formula), not from the separate `strum_dir` field. | `intended_mask` is the actual 7-bit wire byte marvin sent (`FretboardLink_Send` value at [fretboard_link.c:430](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)); distilling against the byte-on-the-wire is the whole point. `strum_dir` is a redundant convenience enum. Using the mask keeps the label = exactly what fretboard saw. |
54	| 2026-06-03 | ACTUATOR producer wiring confirmed present in marvin firmware before building the exporter. | `PerfLog_EmitActuator` is called unconditionally inside `FretboardLink_Send` ([fretboard_link.c:430](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)), which both `timing_pipeline` and `manual_control` drive. So any self-play capture with the `ACTUATOR` (0x0A) mask bit set carries `intended_mask` + `strum_dir` per Send — no firmware work needed for Phase 1. |
55	| 2026-06-03 | Phase 2 windowing slices by **row index** (60 consecutive rows = one 250 ms window), **not** by the CSV `timestamp` column. Proceed assuming a uniform 240 Hz cadence. | The first real capture revealed `FretboardRaw` timestamps are bursty (stamped at marvin's RX/emit time, not at fretboard sample time) — see the open-questions entry. Each row is still exactly one true fretboard sample at the fixed 240 Hz rate, so counting rows gives correct, jitter-free windows; slicing by wall-clock timestamp would not. The `timestamp` column stays useful for plotting/duration only. |
56

61	## Open questions
62	
63	> Phase-1-blocking items first; the design forks for phase 2+ live in [`review.md`](review.md).
64	
65	- **[Future hardware — user wants to pursue] 2 photosensors per fret channel (like the CV detector).** Add a second sensor per fret so each channel sees two points along the note's travel (à la marvin's CV detector). Implications: input grows 5→10 channels (`MODEL_N_IN`, the input ring, the input affine — all parameterised already, but the trained model + `model_weights.h` change); two sensors per fret give the model an explicit *velocity/approach* signal (a note dimming sensor A then B encodes speed + direction), which should sharpen onset timing and could reduce the photo→strum lag ambiguity — possibly even let one model span difficulties (relates to the deferred scroll-speed-sensor idea below). Needs: fretboard HW revision (10 ADC inputs / channel mux), a fret_scan update, a wire-format/`FretboardRaw` bump for 10 channels, re-capture the corpus on the new HW, retrain. Big change; the current 5-sensor model is the baseline it must beat. **Discuss scope before building.**
66	
67	- **[Open follow-up] Red fret is the lone laggard (held-out .890 vs ≥.96 for the others).** Consistent across epochs and was joint-weakest in overfit too, so it's real, not noise. *Not* a corpus-coverage gap — slowride red density (26 %) is mid-pack vs the training songs (24–30 %). Hypotheses to test: (a) single-holdout variance — **rotate the holdout** across all five songs and see if the weak fret tracks the song (variance) or stays red (systemic); (b) neighbour confusion — red sits between green/yellow, so check red's false-positives/negatives against green/yellow activity; (c) `ph_red` channel quality (saturation/standardisation stats). Cheapest first move: rotate-holdout cross-val. Carried as a known caveat into Phase 3; confirm whether it actually costs notes against game score before treating it as blocking.
68	
69	- **Need a real self-play capture to close the Phase-1 gate.** The exporter is verified against synthetic records, but the rollout's Phase-1 "done when" requires inspecting one real captured-gameplay CSV. Required record types in the capture's `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`: `SESSION` + `ACTUATOR` + `FRETBOARD_RAW` (the exporter strictly needs only these three); `DETECTOR` recommended for cross-checking `pressed_mask` vs `intended_mask`. The existing files in [`tools/marvin-perf/captures/`](../../marvin-perf/captures/) are *already-exported detector CSVs*, not raw `.bin` captures, so they can't be re-exported through the actuator path — a fresh raw capture is needed.
70	- **Corpus for Phase 2.** Many songs **at Expert** (single difficulty — see decision log), one held-out song reserved and reused across iterations so per-iteration metrics are comparable.
71	
72	- **[Deferred — not fixing now] Label↔feature pairing crosses two USB directions.** Distinct from the timestamp-burstiness issue above. The label (`PERF_REC_ACTUATOR`) is timestamped when marvin *sends* the command to fretboard; the feature (`FRETBOARD_RAW`) is timestamped when marvin *receives* the sample. The exporter forward-fills one onto the other as if they share a clock, but the two streams travel opposite directions over USB CDC with independent latency + jitter, so the reconstructed "which command was active when this ADC sample was taken" pairing has an unknown, independently-varying skew. (Overlaps the [`review.md`](review.md) "CDC + RTOS jitter in labels" risk, but is sharper: it's a *cross-stream* pairing error, not just emit-time jitter.)
73	  - **Candidate fix (deferred, pairs with the timestamp fix):** have the fretboard frame carry the **actuator bitmask it currently has applied** alongside the ADC scan (and its local sample timestamp). Then (sensor, label) is captured atomically on-device in one 240 Hz tick — no cross-stream join, zero skew. This is also the *most faithful* supervision: it's exactly the function the deployed model replaces (fretboard sees ADC → must emit the bitmask to apply now). marvin stays the teacher; we'd read its command off the wire at the point of truth instead of re-timing it on marvin. Training would then prefer fretboard-reported actuator state over `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR`.
74	  - **Cost:** fretboard wire-format growth + `FretboardRaw` schema add on marvin + a new exporter label source. See fretboard journal open-question #4. **For now we proceed with the marvin-side join** — the skew is bounded (small ms) and was present at runtime too; revisit if Phase 2 shows label noise is the accuracy ceiling (ties to [`review.md` Q4](review.md)).
75	
76	- **[CONFIRMED] Legato fret-hold was the fret-accuracy ceiling.** marvin's timing pipeline suppresses a fret release whenever a queued upcoming note needs that fret ([timing_pipeline.c:263](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L263)) — so across consecutive same-fret notes it holds the fret continuously, and in the gap the photosensor reads bright while the label stays `1` (driven by marvin's note-queue lookahead, not observable from the photo). **Proven by the `--labels=detector-fb` probe** (detector `pressed_mask` frets = clean per-note structure, no legato): on slowride-hard overfit, frets went **0.94→0.99 across the board** and the green→orange gradient flattened (loss 0.13→0.063); strum unchanged (same source). Sustains are safe under a line-263 change because a sustain holds via continuous detector `pressed` (no release edge), never reaching the suppression.
77	  - **But detector-fb is a probe, not the deployable label:** detector `pressed` (y=311) leads the photo dip by ~20 ms and releases ~220 ms *before* the strum, so a model trained on it would release the fret before strumming. Correct *structure*, wrong *timing*.
78	  - **Deployable fix (implemented 2026-06-03):** gated line-263 change in marvin's `timing_pipeline.c` — release a fret between separate notes, hold only when re-needed at/before its scheduled release (back-to-back); sustains untouched. Reflash **marvin only**, re-capture hard, export `actuator-fb` → expect ~0.99 deployable frets at correct strike-line timing. (No fretboard/wire change; `applied_mask` still == the command because there's no lazy actuator yet.)
79	
80	- **[Decided] Final actuation architecture: released commands + lazy fretboard + log the command.** For good play at higher difficulties we want (1) marvin/model to command *released-style* per-note play (clean labels — done via line-263), and (2) a fretboard **lazy actuator** that physically holds a fret across same-fret gaps (releases only on a different non-empty fret command or a no-activity timeout) so fast Expert runs don't thrash release/repress and sustains aren't dropped (a dropped sustain makes the on-screen bar disappear → corrupts the feedback loop). Because the lazy layer makes physical state ≠ command, the training label must then be the **commanded** byte: when lazy lands, add a `commanded_mask` field to the fretboard frame/record (the reserved byte absorbs it; frame 17→18 B, schema v5) and the exporter sources `actuator-fb` labels from it. **Sequencing:** line-263 now (hard mode, `applied_mask` already == command); lazy actuator + `commanded_mask` together as the Expert follow-on. Strum mechanisms (monostable + threshold + weight) already validated — onset p95 ~16.7 ms, clean uniform pulses, glitches→0; recall/precision knee to be set on the consistent line-263 dataset (bias toward recall).
81	
82	- **[Future] 3-state fret actuator (user idea).** Give each fret three states instead of two: *pressed-and-note-active*, *pressed-but-between-notes* (legato hold), and *released*. Would let the label distinguish "this fret is down because a note is here now" from "down only because it's reused soon" — directly encoding the legato hold rather than hiding it. Could be a cleaner supervision target than collapsing to a binary press. Parked until the detector-fb probe tells us whether the binary clean-structure label is enough.
83	
84	- **[Future] Dedicated fret-line (scroll-speed) sensor.** The game highway's bar/measure lines scroll past a fixed point at a frequency that *is* the scroll speed — a direct observable of the one variable (difficulty/scroll-speed) that single-row note sensors can't see. A 6th ADC channel aimed at a column where only the horizontal fret lines pass (not the colored notes) would give the model an explicit scroll-speed signal, potentially letting **one** model generalise across difficulties instead of needing per-difficulty models. Open question whether a tiny model can actually exploit it to adjust strum timing. Pairs with [`review.md` Q1/Q5](review.md) (sensor count/placement). Flag for later; v1 stays Expert-only with the existing 5 channels.
85	
86	- **Measure the photo→strum lag before fixing the window length.** With difficulty fixed, the lag is a constant we can measure (cross-correlate photo dips vs strum events in the real capture) rather than guess. Sizes the causal window precisely and turns [`review.md` Q3](review.md) from a blind sweep into a measurement + a narrow sweep around it. Lag-measurement utility is part of the Phase-2 package.
87	
88	- **[Deferred — not fixing now] Fretboard ADC samples carry no true sample timestamp.** The first real self-play capture ([`tools/marvin-perf/captures/web-20260603-104406.csv`](../../marvin-perf/captures/web-20260603-104406.csv), 251.5 s, 59 958 rows) shows the per-row `timestamp` is **bursty, not uniform 240 Hz**: ~2.9 samples cluster within <0.05 ms, then a >10 ms gap (≈12 ms burst period), with *no* rows near the expected 4.17 ms spacing. Cause: `FretboardRaw.hdr.ts_counter` is stamped at marvin's USB-CDC RX/emit time, not at the fretboard's physical sample instant; the host receives the stream in bursts and the RX task drains buffered frames back-to-back.
89	  - **Consequences:** (1) row-index windowing is mandatory (see decision log); (2) forward-filled command labels can skew by up to one burst (~12 ms / ~3 samples) near command transitions — same effect as the "CDC + RTOS jitter in labels" risk in [`review.md`](review.md); measure its magnitude in Phase 2.
90	  - **Candidate fix (deferred):** have the fretboard MCU stamp each 12-byte data frame with its own sample-time counter and carry it on the wire, so marvin records the *absolute sample-time truth* instead of RX time. That's a fretboard wire-format + firmware change (and a `FretboardRaw` schema add on marvin) — out of scope for now. **For the moment we proceed assuming regular 240 Hz intervals and window by row count.** Revisit if Phase 2 shows the label skew hurts strum-timing accuracy.

32	## Open questions
33	
34	1. **No corruption signalling on the wire.** A bit-flip inside the 5 uint16 payload bytes is silently accepted — only out-of-range start/end bytes are caught. At 500 000 baud over EDBG-CDC this is probably fine, but if we ever see suspect detector behaviour, adding a Fletcher-16 byte (matching marvin's wire format) is a one-byte frame growth.
35	
36	2. **No host→firmware framing.** Command stream is raw bitmask bytes with no start byte. A spurious byte (e.g. line glitch on RX) becomes a button command. Acceptable for now because the line is short and runs over the same EDBG-CDC pair as TX, but worth revisiting if we see ghost presses.

38	3. **T1S link transport — direction, not yet built.** Plan to move the marvin link from the SERCOM1 UART to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY (system spec §6 + [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md)). Fretboard-side cost is an OA TC6 SPI driver + minimal L2 framing (~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM, one free SERCOM in SPI mode + CS_N/IRQ_N/reset GPIO); the 17-byte data frame + 1-byte command formats ride unchanged inside the Ethernet payload, so `data_stream.c`/`cmd_receive.c` need no logic change — only the transport under them swaps. Open sub-items: PLCA-multidrop vs point-to-point (lean PLCA), custom ethertype + the two hardcoded MACs, and whether to keep the UART as a bring-up fallback (decides if SERCOM1's data path is reclaimed). PoDL is transparent to the MCU (zero firmware footprint). Decide before any code lands.

348:- **Live mode**: the server emits a `frame_tick` message on every buffer write (~30 Hz). The browser updates `currentFrame = {seq, t}` and re-clips the chart's leading edge to that `t`. ADC samples that arrived *after* the latest displayed frame are buffered but not yet visible; they are revealed on the next tick. Chart movement is therefore quantized at the camera frame rate, which is the trade-off we accept to keep video, charts, and overlays exactly aligned.
349:- **Pause / scrub**: `frame_tick` is ignored. The user moves `currentFrame` via the timeline, frame-step buttons, or slow-mo playback. Each scrub action returns from the server with a `{seq, t}` pair, which the browser writes back into `currentFrame`.
350:- **CSV / no-camera fallback**: when no camera is attached, no `frame_tick` is emitted. The browser falls back to the latest ingested ADC sample timestamp as `currentFrame.t`, with `seq=null`.

99	## 6. Cross-cutting decisions
100	
101	- **Architecture pivot.** The original PC-hosted / Elgato-USB-capture / PS2 / single-PIC-actuator design is retired. Source documents are preserved at [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/) for design-rationale reference; they are *not* maintained.
102	- **`frame_epoch` is the master sync token.** A 32-bit counter incremented by marvin's video task on every captured ISC frame. Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
103	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw BGR888 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.
104	- **Centralized timing on marvin, with a fretboard-takeover fallback.** marvin runs the chord-window FIFO and strum scheduler by default; an operator-mode toggle hands timing back to fretboard's standalone `fret_button.c` while marvin still records observations.
105	- **Operating modes are independent toggles**, not a global state machine: `detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`. Named modes (idle / calibrate / dry-run / play / replay / record) are presets over them.
106	- **Planned: fretboard ↔ marvin link moves to 10BASE-T1S + dumb PoDL.** Replace the FLEXCOM2/SERCOM UART pair with single-pair Ethernet via a LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY on each end. Motivation, in order: PoDL carries power *and* data on one pair to the guitar; better noise/cable tolerance; PLCA multidrop headroom; and demonstrating 10BASE-T1S + PoDL inside a larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM). Bandwidth is not a driver — the existing UART has ~12× headroom. PoDL is **dumb** (fixed voltage, no SCCP negotiation) and transparent to both MCUs. No IP stack — the host implements only SPI + the OPEN Alliance TC6 chunk protocol + minimal L2 framing, with the existing frame formats riding unchanged inside the Ethernet payload. Fits comfortably on the PIC32CM (est. ~6–10 KB flash / ~1–2 KB SRAM); marvin is bare-metal so it gets a shared portable `oa_tc6` driver, not a free netdev. Detail in [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](docs/t1s-podl-link.md).

128	## 8. What this is *not*
129	
130	To anchor against the original architecture (preserved in `docs/archive/`):
131	
132	- **Not PC-hosted.** marvin is the runtime brain; no host PC is required for play.
133	- **Not USB-capture / Elgato.** Video is captured directly off HDMI via a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 path into the SAM9X75's ISC.
134	- **Not PS2.** The supported console is the Nintendo Wii (with an ElectronWarp component → HDMI converter).
135	- **Not a single-MCU actuator.** Sensing and timing live on marvin; fretboard is a sensor/actuator MCU, not a solo controller (with the explicit exception of the standalone-fallback mode).
136	- **Not OpenCV / Python at runtime.** CV runs natively on the SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5). Python (`fret-tuner`) is a bench tool only.

1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.

8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over a FLEXCOM2 UART link, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35

45	| Fretboard link (FLEXCOM2 USART) | ✅ working; gameplay tested over the original USB CDC host link. Link rewired to a direct FLEXCOM2 UART for the Curiosity Hybrid board (no host-capable USB port); pending on-hardware re-validation. §4.3. |
46	| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO, strum) | ✅ working; end-to-end gameplay tested on Expert and Easy. §4.4. |

123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.

202	
203	## 4. Subsystems
204	
205	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
206	
207	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
208	
209	**What this subsystem owns:**
210	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
211	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
212	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
213	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
214	
215	**What it doesn't own:**
216	- CV processing (§4.2).
217	- Recording / export (§4.6).
218	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
219	
220	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
221	
222	#### 4.2.1 Role
223	
224	This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
225	
226	#### 4.2.2 Detector model
227	
228	A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:
229	
230	- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
231	- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate.
232	
233	Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.
234	
235	#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)
236	
237	```
238	typedef struct {
239	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
240	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
241	    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
242	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
243	    struct {
244	        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
245	        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
246	        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
247	    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
248	} detector_state_t;
249	```
250	
251	Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
252	
253	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
254	
255	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
256	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
257	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
258	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
259	
260	#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
261	
262	`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:
263	
264	- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
265	- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
266	- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
267	
268	#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
269	
270	- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
271	- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)
272	
273	### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅
274	
275	Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)
276	
277	- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). 1-byte bitmask, no framing. `fretboard_link_task` writes the latest mask via `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write`.
278	- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
279	- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
280	
281	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
282	
283	Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:
284	
285	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
286	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
287	- Per-fret release scheduling.
288	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
289	- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.
290	
291	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.
292	
293	### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
294	
295	10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:
296	
297	- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
298	- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
299	- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
300	- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
301	
302	**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
303	
304	### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧
305	
306	#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)
307	
308	1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
309	2. **Replay / sanity check** — let the user (offline) scrub through a recorded session to investigate misses.
310	3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.
311	
312	Live off-device streaming for side-by-side comparison is *not* on the MVP critical path.
313	
314	#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card
315	
316	Recordings are persisted to an SD card via SDMMC + a simple filesystem (FAT32 via Harmony's FILE_SYSTEM service). The card is removed and read on a workstation; no live network path is required for MVP.
317	
318	Bandwidth ceiling: SDMMC sustained write ≥ 5 MB/s on Class-10 cards is reliably achievable. The recording format below is sized to land well below that.
319	
320	#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes
321	
322	A recording is a **directory** on the SD card, containing:
323	
324	```
325	recordings/
326	└── 2026-05-20T14-32-08/
327	    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
328	    ├── state.bin              // dense detector_state_t records, all detectors, all frames
329	    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
330	    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
331	    └── keyframes/
332	        ├── 000000.bgr         // raw BGR888 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
333	        ├── 000060.bgr
334	        └── ...
335	```
336	
337	- **`state.bin`** — append-only, fixed-size `detector_state_t` records (§4.2.3). At 60 Hz × 2 detectors × ~28 B = ~3.4 KB/s. Trivial.
338	- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
339	- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 12-byte frames at 240 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~2.9 KB/s. Modest. Until the SD recorder lands, the same data is available live as `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (28 B framed) in any marvin-perf capture (default-disabled; enable with `set-mask`).
340	- **Keyframes** — raw BGR888 packed dump every N captured frames. At 720×480 × 3 B = 1.04 MB/keyframe. Default cadence: **1 keyframe per second** (60-frame stride) → 1.04 MB/s sustained. Configurable (every 30 / 60 / 120 / 600 frames). At 1 fps a 5-minute session is ~312 MB — comfortable on any modern SD card.
341	- No software JPEG / video encode. SAM9X75 has no hardware JPEG; CPU encode at 60 fps is infeasible. Keyframes stay raw; offline tools can transcode if desired.
342	
343	Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.
344	
345	#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`
346	
347	A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.
348	
349	For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.
350	
351	#### 4.6.5 manifest.json
352	
353	Minimum fields:
354	
355	```json
356	{
357	  "schema_version": 1,
358	  "session_started_utc": "2026-05-20T14:32:08Z",
359	  "marvin_firmware_git": "<hash>",
360	  "capture": { "width": 720, "height": 480, "fps": 60, "format": "BGR888" },
361	  "keyframe_stride_frames": 60,
362	  "detectors": [
363	    { "id": "cv_marvin_v1", "version": "1.0.0", "calibration": { ... } },
364	    { "id": "adc_fretboard", "version": "1.0.0", "thresholds": { ... } }
365	  ],
366	  "timing": { "chord_window_ms": 20, "strum_delay_ms": 220, "fret_early_ms": 50, "strum_pulse_ms": 50 },
367	  "ended_utc": null
368	}
369	```
370	
371	Written at session start; `ended_utc` is patched on a clean stop.
372	
373	#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
374	
375	A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.04 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
376	
377	If the SD write FIFO falls behind (rare; only a sustained-throughput problem), the recorder drops keyframes (logs a `RECORD_DROP` event into `state.bin`'s metadata channel) but **never** drops detector-state records.
378	
379	#### 4.6.7 Off-board detectors recording independently
380	
381	When a future Edge-AI detection unit is brought online, it can:
382	
383	- Subscribe to marvin's `frame_epoch` over a chosen link (UART/Ethernet/etc.).
384	- Record its own observations (e.g. its own sensor data + its own detector output) in its own format, *keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch`*.
385	- Be aligned post-hoc against marvin's reference recording during training.
386	
387	The spec does not constrain how off-board detectors store their data — only the sync contract (`frame_epoch` timeline) is canonical.
388	
389	#### 4.6.8 On-demand full-frame snapshot (USB CDC) ✅
390	
391	Independent of the SD recording path above (M4, not started), marvin can export a single full-resolution frame on demand over the existing perf-log USB CDC link. The host sends `PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT`; the perf-drain task copies the current frame once into a staging buffer and streams it back as a top-to-bottom run of full-width `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT` band records (each ≤ `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`), all sharing one `frame_epoch`, the last flagged `PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. Bands are written straight to the sink (bypassing the small strip pool) and paced by the wire; emit is not gated by the STRIP type mask. `marvin-perf snapshot` reassembles and saves the frame (`.bgr` + sidecar `.json`, plus `.png` via Pillow). This is the offline-study on-ramp for the game-state work (§4.8) — no in-runtime role.
392	
393	### 4.7 System services 🚧
394	
395	Cross-cutting services not owned by any one subsystem:
396	
397	- **Logging** ✅ severity-filtered printf shim (commit `a79042f`).
398	- **Time** ✅ TC0 / SYS_TIME for OSAL.
399	- **Config persistence** 🚧 calibration values, mode toggles, last-used recording stride. Storage TBD (a config file on SD vs internal flash).
400	- **Watchdog** 🚧 not yet enabled.
401	- **OTA** ⚪ out of scope for now.
402	
403	### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
404	
405	Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
406	
407	#### 4.8.1 Role
408	
409	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
410	
411	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
412	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
413	
414	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
415	
416	Recognition is being bootstrapped offline: the on-demand snapshot path (§4.6.8) collects a corpus of real GH3 screens, the detection algorithms (screen classification, then number/letter/score region readers) are prototyped host-side in Python against that corpus, and only the proven, simple GH3-specific logic is then ported into the firmware `gameplay_engine` module. Per Q10, the approach favors fixed-region/color/glyph matching over general CV — GH3's screens, fonts, and layouts are static.
417	
418	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
419	
420	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
421	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
422	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
423	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
424	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
425	
426	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
427	
428	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
429	
430	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
431	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
432	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
433	
434	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
435	
436	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
437	
438	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
439	
440	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
441	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
442	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
443	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
444	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
445	
446	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
447	
448	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
449	
450	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
451	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
452	
453	### 4.9 Operator command console ✅
454	
455	An **interactive text console** over **FLEXCOM2 USART (115 200 8N1, ring-buffer mode)** — marvin's `PA13` (FLEXCOM2_IO0, `CLI_TX`) / `PA14` (FLEXCOM2_IO1, `CLI_RX`) — deliberately on a separate channel from the DBGU log/printf chatter — log output stays on DBGU, console I/O stays on FLEXCOM2, so neither pollutes the other.
456	
457	- **Why not Harmony `SYS_CONSOLE`/`SYS_COMMAND`:** those are MCC-config-coupled and live in regenerated files (this board already carries ~10 re-apply patches against clobbered generated code). The console is instead a small in-tree module (`console/console.{h,c}`) in the same shape as `fretboard_link`/`perf_log`: it owns the USART plib directly, is fully statically allocated, and is kept out of MCC via `user.cmake`.
458	- **Library:** [embedded-cli](https://github.com/funbiscuit/embedded-cli) (vendored under `default/src/third_party/embedded-cli/`, MIT), used in static-allocation mode (a fixed `CLI_UINT` buffer → no `malloc`). Provides line editing, history, and tab-completion.
459	- **Mechanics:** one FreeRTOS task drains the FLEXCOM2 RX ring (woken by a 1-byte read-threshold notification, like `fretboard_rx_task`), feeds bytes to embedded-cli, and runs the dispatcher. Output is written byte-by-byte into the TX ring.
460	- **Commands (v0):** `status`, `detect <cv|adc> <on|off>`, `active <cv|adc>`, `timing <on|off>`, `manual <on|off>`, `fret <g|r|y|b|o> <0|1>`, `strum <down|up>` — dispatching into the existing `Detector_*`, `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled`, and `ManualControl_*` setters. The binding table is a plain static array; adding a command is one row. Maps onto the §6 operating-mode toggles. (`record`/`game_*` toggles and runtime timing-constant setters are deferred until those subsystems / setters exist.)
461	
462	---
463	
464	## 5. External interfaces 🚧
465	
466	To be expanded once §4.3 (fretboard wire protocol) is settled. Will document:
467	
468	- Marvin ↔ fretboard UART framing, byte-for-byte.
469	- Recording on-disk binary layouts (the `_t` structs from §4.2.3 and §4.6 in canonical form, including endianness).
470	- USB-CDC dev console framing (if any), Ethernet ref-data stream framing (if/when added).
471	
472	## 6. Operating modes 🚧
473	
474	Default model: independent toggles (matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split). Confirmed direction; concrete toggle list:
475	
476	| Toggle | Effect |
477	|---|---|
478	| `detect_enable` | CV + ADC detectors run; detector-state bus is active. |
479	| `marvin_timing_enable` | marvin's chord FIFO / strum scheduler runs. When off, fretboard runs its own pipeline (§4.4 fallback). |
480	| `actuate_enable` | Commands are actually sent to fretboard. When off, marvin computes commands but suppresses them (dry-run). |
481	| `record_enable` | Recording task writes to SD. |
482	| `game_observe_enable` | Game-state observer task runs; `xGameStateQueue` is active. |
483	| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |
484	
485	A handful of named composite modes (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record) are presets over these toggles. Replay specifically requires loading a prior recording from SD and playing detector-state events back through the timing pipeline against the original keyframes — UI affordance for that comes later.
486	
487	## 7. Build & deploy 🚧
488	
489	To be filled. Topics: MCC-clobbered files (which paths are safe to edit by hand vs. regenerate), `user.cmake` boundaries, flashing workflow, sequence of MCC steps to reproduce the project.
490	
491	## 8. Phasing & milestones 🚧
492	
493	Proposed order; each is a buildable demo:
494	
495	1. **M1 — Reference detector v0** (§4.2). One CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` to the bus. No actuation. Proves the bus and the detection task structure.
496	2. **M2 — Fretboard link** (§4.3). UART up; ADC stream ingested; `adc_fretboard` detector publishing onto the bus alongside `cv_marvin_v1`.
497	3. **M3 — Timing pipeline + actuation** (§4.4). Chord FIFO + strum scheduling; commands sent over UART; fretboard actuates. End-to-end play possible.
498	4. **M4 — Recording to SD** (§4.6). SDMMC + FAT mount; record task writes state/commands/ADC/keyframes during a session.
499	5. **M5 — Operator UI v0** (§4.5). Live view with overlays; mode toggles. UI framework decided here.
500	6. **M6 — Calibration UI** (§4.5). Per-fret ROI placement + threshold tuning on the device.
501	7. **M7 — Replay** (§6). Load a recording from SD, replay through the timing pipeline.
502	8. **M8 — Standalone-fretboard fallback** (§4.4). Marvin-disabled-pipeline mode validated.
503	9. **M9 — Game-state observer v0** (§4.8). Recognize main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score states; surface as `xGameStateQueue` events. No control yet.
504	10. **M10 — Game-state control v0** (§4.8). High-level verbs ("start single-player song X") drive menu navigation through the same fretboard link.
505	
506	Live-stream Ethernet, Edge-AI integration, and config-on-flash are post-M8.
507	
508	## 9. Open questions
509	
510	| # | Question | Status |
511	|---|---|---|
512	| Q1 | Reference-data format details — keyframe stride and per-fret patch sizes if patches are added later. | Direction set (§4.6.3); exact stride defaults to 60 frames, revisit after first training-data consumer exists. |
513	| Q2 | Reference-data transport beyond SD — Ethernet live stream timing. | Deferred post-M8. |
514	| Q3 | Detector-state bus shape — typed messages on a queue (§4.2.4) is the working choice; revisit if multi-consumer latency becomes a problem. | Working choice. |
515	| Q4 | Timing pipeline location — marvin centralized with fretboard fallback. | Settled; implementation in M3 + M8. |
516	| Q5 | UI framework — Legato vs custom on GFX2D. | Open. Decide at M5. |
517	| Q6 | Operating-mode model — independent toggles. | Settled (§6). |
518	| Q7 | Fret-tuner's long-term fate — survives as off-band dev/calibration tool. | Settled; not in runtime path. |
519	| Q8 | Initial CV algorithm choice for `cv_marvin_v1`. | Open. Decide at M1. |
520	| Q9 | Config persistence location (SD file vs internal flash). | Open. Decide at M4 alongside SDMMC bring-up. |
521	| Q10 | Game-state recognizer algorithm — template matching vs OCR vs color/region heuristics vs small CNN. | Open. Decide at M9; revisit if first algorithm misclassifies on real game UI. |
522	| Q11 | Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline (§4.4 vs §4.8). Default working assumption: mutually exclusive (controller runs only outside `gameplay` state); may need richer arbitration if a game has gameplay-screen menus or pause overlays we want to drive. | Open. Decide at M10. |
