```text
1	# Fret-Tuner Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Web-based Python tool for developing and refining fret-press detection algorithms. Consumes the same raw ADC data the firmware sees -- either live from the board over UART or replayed from a captured CSV -- runs detection logic in Python, and visualizes everything in an interactive browser UI. Optionally sends actuation commands back to the microcontroller, moving the entire detection and strum-timing pipeline to the PC for rapid iteration.
6	
7	## Video reference (always-on)
8	
9	A first-class always-on subsystem. The UI exposes a video viewport at all times; behavior is independent of which detector is active.
10	
11	**Primary role**: time-aligned visual reference and recording against the ADC sample timeline and any derived signals (waveforms, detector state, fret/strum events). The question it answers: does what was on screen at time *t* match what the ADC and algorithms reported at *t*?
12	
13	**Secondary roles**: debugging alignment between capture and charts, reviewing a session after the fact, documenting false positives/negatives.
14	
15	### Requirements
16	
17	- **Primacy**: video reference is a first-class always-on subsystem, not gated on detector choice.
18	- **Source ownership**: the fret-tuner **backend** owns the camera. Exactly one source feeds the reference ring buffer at a time. The source is selectable in the UI from cameras enumerated by the backend, plus a "none" option, plus any video file supplied for replay.
19	- **Buffer**: server-side ring buffer with **≥30 s wall-clock coverage** at a **target 30 Hz** capture rate. The buffer accepts whatever rate the camera delivers, sized to retain ≥30 s even when the source runs as fast as 60 Hz.
20	- **Synchronization**: every buffered frame carries a sample-clock timestamp anchored to the ADC stream so that any time *t* in the chart timeline maps to the closest buffered frame.
21	- **Live behavior**: while playing, the browser shows the most recent server frame with overlays composed for that frame's *t*.
22	- **Paused / scrubbing**: when paused, or while panning/zooming the charts, the video display follows the chart cursor / center time, picking the closest buffered frame.
23	- **Overlays**: per-frame composition (live and paused) at the display path's natural rate. Required minimum set:
24	    - 5 fret **pressed-state** indicators (per ADC channel)
25	    - **strum state** indicators (down + up, sourced from the actuator pipeline)
26	    - **scrub-time** text cursor
27	  Detectors may register additional overlay layers via the extension hook (see [Detection Algorithm Contract → Overlay extension](#overlay-extension)).
28	- **Detector consumption**: detectors that need pixel data (e.g. `detect_video`) **read from the reference buffer**; they do not own a separate camera grab.
29	
30	## Actuation (always-on)
31	
32	A first-class always-on subsystem that owns the GPIO command serial link to the actuator microcontroller. Behavior is independent of which detector is active and of where the ADC data comes from (live serial, CSV replay, or none).
33	
34	**Primary role**: consume detector state each tick, run the strum timing pipeline (chord window, FIFO scheduling, fret early/late, strum pulse), and emit a 1-byte GPIO bitmask to the actuator board over UART.
35	
36	### Requirements
37	
38	- **Primacy**: actuation is a first-class always-on subsystem, not a side effect of opening a data port. It can be enabled with any detector and any data source (including CSV-only replay against a live actuator board).
39	- **Source ownership**: the actuator owns its own `serial.Serial` handle. The port is selectable in the UI from ports enumerated by the backend, plus a "none" option.
40	- **Port sharing**: the actuator port may name the same `/dev/cu.*` device as an ADC data port (single-board case). In that case the backend opens the device once and shares the handle between the data reader and the actuator writer; the writer never blocks on the reader and vice versa.
41	- **Reconnect**: when the actuator port is lost (unplug, USB sleep, etc.) the writer goes silent without raising; on reconnect, output resumes. Auto-reconnect runs at the same cadence as the data-port reconnect.
42	- **Enable gate**: a UI toggle gates output at the *bitmask* level. When disabled, the timing pipeline still runs (and reports `output_mask = 0`), but no bytes are written. Manual GPIO override (`manual_output`) still works when actuation is disabled, so individual buttons can be poked from the browser without engaging the full pipeline.
43	- **Always-on lifecycle**: created at server startup, persists across detector switches, never owned by a detector.
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	The backend is organized around two **always-on subsystems** (video reference, actuation) and one swappable **detector subsystem**. Always-on subsystems own their I/O and run regardless of which detector is active. The detector consumes whatever inputs it needs (ADC stream, video frames, etc.), produces detection state, and feeds it to the actuator.
48	
49	```
50	Browser (localhost:8080)
51	  ├── Video viewport (live or scrubbed frame + composited overlays)
52	  ├── uPlot charts (zoom, pan, pause)
53	  ├── Controls (camera source, actuator port, detector, params, recording)
54	  └── WebSocket  (sample data, detector state, sources, actuator status)
55	        ↕
56	FastAPI backend (Python)
57	  ├── camera.py          (OpenCV capture → shared ring buffer, ≥30 s @ ≥30 Hz)   [always-on]
58	  ├── actuator.py        (strum timing pipeline + GPIO serial TX)                 [always-on]
59	  ├── stream.py          (serial/CSV ADC source for ADC-based detectors)
60	  ├── detect_*.py        (consume samples and/or video frames; emit overlay layers)
61	  └── server.py          (WebSocket + HTTP video transport, subsystem wiring)
62	        ↕
63	Microcontrollers (PIC32CM)
64	  ├── Data board   →  fret_scan + data_stream     (12-byte ADC frames over UART)
65	  └── Actuator board → cmd_receive                (1-byte bitmask → GPIO assert/release)
66	                       The data board and actuator board may be the same physical
67	                       device sharing one UART, or two different devices.
68	```
69	
70	Browser and backend are deployed as a split / resizable layout: video viewport and ADC charts are co-equal, neither dominant by default. The shared video ring buffer lives in the backend; detector pixel consumers and the browser display both read from it.
71	
72	## File Layout
73	
74	```
75	tools/fret-tuner/
76	    fret-tuner.py          # CLI entry point (launches server, opens browser)
77	    server.py              # FastAPI app, WebSocket, data pipeline wiring
78	    camera.py              # OpenCV capture + shared video ring buffer
79	    index.html             # Browser UI (uPlot charts + video viewport, no build step)
80	    stream.py              # Serial + CSV data sources
81	    actuator.py            # Strum timing pipeline (port of fret_button.c)
82	    detect_threshold.py    # Detection: fixed per-channel hysteresis
83	    detect_trough.py       # Detection: baseline + trough FSM
84	    detect_slope.py        # Detection: EMA + slope FSM with re-press handling
85	    detect_video.py        # Detection: pixel sampling against the reference buffer
86	    video_calibrate.py     # Standalone helper for marking detect_video sensor coords
87	    requirements.txt       # Python dependencies
88	    SPEC.md                # This file
89	    .gitignore
90	
91	firmware/fretboard/
92	    cmd_receive.c          # UART RX command handler
93	    cmd_receive.h          # Header
94	```
95	
96	## Data Source
97	
98	### UART Binary Frame (micro → PC)
99	
100	The fretboard firmware streams 12-byte packed frames at **240 Hz** over SERCOM1 USART at **500000 baud** (8N1):
101	
102	```
103	Offset  Size   Field
104	------  -----  -----
105	0       1      Start byte (0x03)
106	1       2      Green   (uint16 LE, 12-bit ADC)
107	3       2      Red     (uint16 LE)
108	5       2      Yellow  (uint16 LE)
109	7       2      Blue    (uint16 LE)
110	9       2      Orange  (uint16 LE)
111	11      1      End byte (0xFC)
112	```
113	
114	### Command Byte (PC → micro)
115	
116	Single byte bitmask sent over the same serial connection (full-duplex). Each bit directly controls one GPIO output:
117	
118	```
119	Bit   Output
120	---   ------
121	0     Green fret
122	1     Red fret
123	2     Yellow fret
124	3     Blue fret
125	4     Orange fret
126	5     Strum down
127	6     Strum up
128	```
129	
130	Bit = 1 → assert (drive low). Bit = 0 → release (tri-state). The firmware applies the latest received byte each tick. When no bytes are received, outputs remain unchanged.
131	
132	### Serial Auto-Reconnect
133	
134	When the USB serial connection is lost (board unplugged, USB sleep, etc.), the feed loop catches the error, closes the stale serial handle, and retries opening the port every 2 seconds until the device reappears. On disconnect and reconnect, the server pushes `serial_status` messages over WebSocket so the browser UI can display the current state (amber "Serial disconnected -- reconnecting..." while down, green "Connected" on recovery). CSV replay sources are not affected.
135	
136	### CSV Replay Format
137	
138	CSV files captured from Microchip Data Visualizer. Expected columns:
139	
140	```
141	timestamp,BLUE RAW,BLUE,GREEN RAW,GREEN,ORANGE RAW,ORANGE,RED RAW,RED,YELLOW RAW,YELLOW
142	```
143	
144	Only the `timestamp` and `* RAW` columns are consumed.
145	
146	## Detection Algorithm Contract
147	
148	Each detector lives in its own `detect_*.py` file and exports a `Detector` class:
149	
150	```python
151	class Detector:
152	    @classmethod
153	    def default_params(cls) -> dict:
154	        """Return default parameter values."""
155	
156	    def __init__(self, **params):
157	        """Accept tunable parameters as keyword args."""
158	
159	    def update(self, sample: Sample) -> dict:
160	        """Process one sample. Return per-channel state dict:
161	        {
162	            "green":  {"pressed": bool, "baseline": int, ...},
163	            ...
164	        }
165	        """
166	```
167	
168	The `update()` return dict must include `"pressed"` (bool) and `"baseline"` (int) per channel. Additional keys are detector-specific and available for charting.
169	
170	The server auto-injects `"raw"` (the raw ADC reading for that channel) into each per-channel state dict before charting, so detectors do not need to copy it themselves.
171	
172	### Chart schema
173	
174	Detectors describe what their five chart slots should display via:
175	
176	```python
177	class Detector:
178	    def chart_schema(self) -> list[dict]:
179	        """Return 5 slot specs:
180	        {
181	            "id":      str,             # state-dict key (e.g. "green")
182	            "label":   str,             # axis label
183	            "color":   "#rrggbb",
184	            "y_range": [min, max],
185	            "series":  [
186	                {"key": str, "label": str, "color": "#rrggbb",
187	                 "width": float, "dash": [int, int] | None},
188	                ...
189	            ],
190	        }
191	        """
192	```
193	
194	Each `series.key` names a field inside that channel's state dict. `stream.adc_chart_schema(extra_series=[...])` builds the conventional `raw + <extras>` layout for ADC detectors. Detectors with no use for raw ADC (e.g. `detect_video`) simply omit the `"raw"` series.
195	
196	The browser rebuilds its chart slots whenever a new schema arrives, so switching detectors swaps the chart contents (labels, colors, y-range, plotted series) along with the algorithm.
197	
198	### Overlay extension
199	
200	Detectors may optionally contribute named overlay layers to the video viewport:
201	
202	```python
203	class Detector:
204	    def overlays(self) -> list[OverlayLayer]:
205	        """Optional. Return list of overlay layers to draw on the video.
206	        Each layer = {name: str, draw(ctx, frame_meta, sample_state) -> None}.
207	        Returning [] (or omitting the method) means no detector-specific overlays.
208	        """
209	        return []
210	```
211	
212	Layers compose on top of the always-on minimum set (fret pressed-state, strum state, scrub time). Transport for overlay drawcalls is implementation-defined: the server may bake them into delivered frames, or stream drawcall metadata (see [WebSocket Protocol](#websocket-protocol) `video_meta`) for client-side compositing.
213	
214	`detect_video`, for example, registers a layer that draws its sensor sample points and per-button signal levels.
215	
216	### Adding a new detector
217	
218	1. Create `tools/fret-tuner/detect_myalgo.py`
219	2. Implement a `Detector` class following the contract above
220	3. Select it from the dropdown in the browser UI (or `--detector detect_myalgo` on the CLI)
221	
222	The server hot-reloads detector modules on switch, so you can edit the file and switch to it without restarting.
223	
224	## Bundled Detector: detect_threshold
225	
226	Fixed per-channel hysteresis. Matches the current firmware `fret_detect.c`.
227	
228	| Parameter | Default | Description |
229	|-----------|---------|-------------|
230	| `GREEN_PRESS` | 2500 | Green press threshold |
231	| `GREEN_RELEASE` | 2800 | Green release threshold |
232	| `RED_PRESS` | 2500 | Red press threshold |
233	| `RED_RELEASE` | 2800 | Red release threshold |
234	| `YELLOW_PRESS` | 1500 | Yellow press threshold |
235	| `YELLOW_RELEASE` | 1700 | Yellow release threshold |
236	| `BLUE_PRESS` | 1500 | Blue press threshold |
237	| `BLUE_RELEASE` | 1700 | Blue release threshold |
238	| `ORANGE_PRESS` | 2000 | Orange press threshold |
239	| `ORANGE_RELEASE` | 2200 | Orange release threshold |
240	
241	## Bundled Detector: detect_trough
242	
243	Baseline + trough FSM. Three states: IDLE → DESCENDING → PRESSED.
244	
245	| Parameter | Default | Description |
246	|-----------|---------|-------------|
247	| `MIN_DROP` | 200 | ADC counts below baseline to begin descent tracking |
248	| `RISE_CONFIRM` | 50 | ADC counts above running minimum to confirm press |
249	| `RELEASE_MARGIN` | 300 | Counts within baseline to trigger release |
250	| `BASELINE_DECAY_RATE` | 250 | Samples between 1-count baseline decrements |
251	
252	## Actuator (actuator.py)
253	
254	Python port of `firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c`. Translates detector press/release edges into a timed sequence of fret assertions and strum pulses.
255	
256	### Timing Pipeline
257	
258	1. **Chord window** -- new presses within `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` are accumulated
259	2. **Chord commit** -- schedules note assert at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS - FRET_EARLY_MS` and strum at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS`
260	3. **Note FIFO** (cap 8) -- pending fret assertions, processed in order
261	4. **Strum FIFO** (cap 8) -- pending strum triggers, alternating up/down
262	5. **Strum pulse** -- held for `STRUM_PULSE_MS`, then released
263	6. **Delayed releases** -- each released fret is scheduled for release at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS`, skipped if still needed by pending notes/strums
264	
265	### Timing Parameters
266	
267	| Parameter | Default | Description |
268	|-----------|---------|-------------|
269	| `STRUM_DELAY_MS` | 220 | Delay from chord commit to strum |
270	| `FRET_EARLY_MS` | 50 | How early frets assert before strum |
271	| `STRUM_PULSE_MS` | 50 | How long the strum output is held |
272	| `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` | 20 | Window for accumulating chord presses |
273	
274	All timing is driven by sample timestamps, not wall clock, so the pipeline behaves identically in live and CSV replay modes.
275	
276	### Output
277	
278	Computes a 7-bit bitmask each tick and writes it to the serial port. Actuation is disabled by default and toggled from the browser UI.
279	
280	## Firmware: cmd_receive
281	
282	Minimal command receiver added to the fretboard firmware. Replaces `fret_detect` and `fret_button` in `main.c` -- the microcontroller becomes a scan/stream/actuate relay.
283	
284	### Main loop (modified)
285	
286	```c
287	fret_scan_all();
288	data_stream_send();
289	cmd_receive_update();
290	```
291	
292	### cmd_receive_update()
293	
294	1. Checks `SERCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet()` for available bytes
295	2. Reads all available bytes, keeps the last one
296	3. Applies the bitmask: for each bit, asserts (drive low + output enable) or releases (input enable) the corresponding GPIO
297	
298	## Browser UI
299	
300	Single-file HTML served by the backend at `http://localhost:8080`. Loads uPlot from CDN (no build step).
301	
302	### Charts
303	
304	- 5 stacked uPlot time-series charts, one per fret slot (green, red, yellow, blue, orange)
305	- The active detector's `chart_schema()` defines the series, labels, colors, and y-range for each slot. ADC detectors plot raw ADC + their baseline / threshold lines; `detect_video` plots its hold + edge signals (no raw ADC). Switching detectors swaps the chart contents.
306	- Shaded press bands and (where the detector emits `press_count`) re-press tick marks are overlaid in the slot color
307	- Native mouse-drag zoom, scroll-wheel zoom, double-click to reset
308	
309	### Controls (sidebar)
310	
311	- **Pause / Resume** -- freezes chart updates; data continues to buffer server-side
312	- **Window width** -- slider controlling visible time range (0.5--30 seconds)
313	- **Detector dropdown** -- switch between available `detect_*.py` modules live
314	- **Parameter sliders** -- dynamically generated from the active detector's `default_params()`, changes take effect immediately
315	- **Camera source dropdown** -- enumerated cameras + "none"; controls the always-on video reference
316	- **Actuator port dropdown** -- enumerated `/dev/cu.*` (or platform equivalent) serial ports + "none"; controls the always-on actuator. Selecting the same device as a live ADC data port shares the handle.
317	- **Actuation toggle** -- enable/disable writing command bytes (the timing pipeline runs either way)
318	- **Timing sliders** -- strum delay, fret early, strum pulse, chord window
319	- **Connection status** indicators -- separate badges for the data port and the actuator port
320	
321	### Layout
322	
323	Split / resizable two-pane layout. The **video viewport** and the **ADC charts** are co-equal first-class panes; neither is dominant by default and the user can resize the split. Sidebar controls remain to one side.
324	
325	### Video viewport
326	
327	Backed by the always-on subsystem in [Video reference (always-on)](#video-reference-always-on). UI surface:
328	
329	- **Source selector** -- lists cameras enumerated by the backend, plus "none" and any `--video FILE` replay file. Selection persisted by the backend, applied immediately.
330	- **Recording controls** -- start / stop / save buffer (writes paired video + ADC log; see [Recording & paired CSV replay](#recording--paired-csv-replay)). Default off.
331	- **Pause / scrub** -- synchronized with the charts' pause; chart center time drives the displayed frame.
332	- **Overlays** -- always-on minimum (5 fret pressed-state indicators, strum state, scrub time) plus any layers the active detector registers via [Overlay extension](#overlay-extension).
333	
334	### Recording & paired CSV replay
335	
336	- A live session can be **recorded**: the backend drains the reference ring buffer to a video file alongside the ADC sample log (CSV), with a shared time anchor written into the recording so the two replay in sync.
337	- `python fret-tuner.py --csv FILE [--video FILE]` replays both. If `--video` is omitted, the video viewport shows "no recorded video for this CSV" and disables source selection for the duration of the replay.
338	- Recording is started/stopped explicitly from the sidebar; default off.
339	
340	### WebSocket Protocol
341	
342	Sample data, detector state, and overlay metadata flow over the WebSocket; raw video frames are delivered over a parallel HTTP video transport (implementation choice; the existing tool uses MJPEG). Both share the same sample-clock timestamps so chart and video scrubbing target the same *t*.
343	
344	#### Master clock: the displayed video frame
345	
346	The currently displayed video frame is the single source of truth for *now*. Each captured frame has a `seq` (monotonic id) and a `t` (sample-clock timestamp), and every UI element (chart cursor, viewport scroll, overlay text) aligns to the *currently displayed* frame's `t` -- not to the latest ADC sample, the wall clock, or the network arrival time.
347	
348	- **Live mode**: the server emits a `frame_tick` message on every buffer write (~30 Hz). The browser updates `currentFrame = {seq, t}` and re-clips the chart's leading edge to that `t`. ADC samples that arrived *after* the latest displayed frame are buffered but not yet visible; they are revealed on the next tick. Chart movement is therefore quantized at the camera frame rate, which is the trade-off we accept to keep video, charts, and overlays exactly aligned.
349	- **Pause / scrub**: `frame_tick` is ignored. The user moves `currentFrame` via the timeline, frame-step buttons, or slow-mo playback. Each scrub action returns from the server with a `{seq, t}` pair, which the browser writes back into `currentFrame`.
350	- **CSV / no-camera fallback**: when no camera is attached, no `frame_tick` is emitted. The browser falls back to the latest ingested ADC sample timestamp as `currentFrame.t`, with `seq=null`.
351	
352	Server → client:
353	
354	```json
355	{"type": "data", "samples": [...], "state": [...], "actuator_mask": 0}
356	{"type": "frame_tick", "seq": 1234, "t": 12.345}          // ~30 Hz, camera only
357	{"type": "detector", "name": "...", "params": {...}, "available": [...],
358	 "timing": {...}, "actuate_enabled": false}
359	{"type": "serial_status", "connected": true}              // data port
360	{"type": "actuator_status", "connected": true,
361	 "available": [...], "active": "/dev/cu.usbmodem21202"}   // actuator port
362	{"type": "video_meta", "t": 12.345, "layers": [...]}
363	{"type": "sources", "available": [...], "active": "..."}  // camera sources
364	{"type": "recording", "active": false, "path": null}
365	```
366	
367	Client → server:
368	
369	```json
370	{"type": "pause"}
371	{"type": "resume"}
372	{"type": "set_params", "params": {"KEY": value}}
373	{"type": "set_detector", "name": "detect_trough"}
374	{"type": "set_timing", "params": {"STRUM_DELAY_MS": 200}}
375	{"type": "set_actuate", "enabled": true}
376	{"type": "set_source", "name": "..."}            // camera source
377	{"type": "set_actuator_port", "name": "/dev/cu.usbmodem21202"}  // or "none"
378	{"type": "manual_output", "mask": 0}
379	{"type": "record_start"}
380	{"type": "record_stop"}
381	```
382	
383	The backend also exposes:
384	
385	- `GET /api/sources` -- camera sources (mirror of the WS `sources` message)
386	- `GET /api/serial-ports` -- enumerated serial ports for the actuator dropdown
387	- `GET /video` -- live MJPEG of the working-resolution buffer (server-rendered overlays applied)
388	- `GET /video/snap?t=<sec>` -- single JPEG of the buffered frame closest to *t*. Response carries `X-Frame-Seq` and `X-Frame-Time` headers (and a matching `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`) so the browser can sync `currentFrame` to the snapped frame even when the snapped *t* differs from the requested *t*.
389	- `GET /video/step?dir=next|prev&n=N&{seq=S | t=T}` -- walk the ring buffer to the n-th next/prev frame. Address by `seq` for exact stepping (preferred when the browser holds a known frame); fall back to `t` for the first scrub when seq is unknown. Returns `{"seq": int, "t": float, "buffered": int}`.
390	
391	## CLI Reference
392	
393	```
394	usage: fret-tuner.py [-h] (--port PORT | --csv FILE) [--video FILE]
395	                     [--actuator-port PORT] [--camera ID]
396	                     [--detector MODULE] [--param KEY=VALUE] [--fast]
397	                     [--host HOST] [--web-port PORT]
398	```
399	
400	`--port` selects the **data** serial port (ADC frame source). `--actuator-port` selects the **actuator** serial port; if omitted, the actuator starts idle and a port can be chosen at runtime from the sidebar dropdown. If `--actuator-port` names the same device as `--port`, the backend opens it once and shares the handle for read and write.
401	
402	### Examples
403	
404	```bash
405	# Single board: ADC stream + actuator on the same port (handle is shared)
406	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 \
407	    --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202
408	
409	# Two boards: ADC stream on one device, actuator on another
410	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 \
411	    --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem31301
412	
413	# CSV replay against a live actuator board
414	python fret-tuner.py --csv session.csv --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem31301
415	
416	# CSV replay, no actuator (UI dropdown can attach one later)
417	python fret-tuner.py --csv ../../firmware/fretboard/fretboard-sample-raw.csv
418	
419	# Start with trough detector and custom parameters
420	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 --detector detect_trough \
421	    --param MIN_DROP=150 --param RISE_CONFIRM=30
422	
423	# Fast CSV replay (no real-time pacing)
424	python fret-tuner.py --csv capture.csv --fast
425	```
426	
427	## Dependencies
428	
429	Uses the repo-level `.venv` (Python 3.12). Required packages:
430	
431	- `pyserial >= 3.5`
432	- `numpy >= 1.24`
433	- `fastapi >= 0.115`
434	- `uvicorn[standard] >= 0.30`
435	- `websockets >= 12.0`
436	- `opencv-python` (server-side video capture and `detect_video`)
437	
438	## Bundled Detector: detect_video
439	
440	Pixel-sampling detector that **consumes the shared reference video buffer**. It does not own a camera and does not serve its own video stream; sensor sample points and per-button signal levels are exposed as an [overlay layer](#overlay-extension) for the viewport.
441	
442	Two sensor points per button, both above the strike line:
443	
444	- **Sensor 1 (hold)** -- brightness detect (color OR white). Sets `pressed=True` whenever max channel brightness exceeds `THRESHOLD`.
445	- **Sensor 2 (edge)** -- color-filtered leading-edge detect. Increments `press_count` on each new note arrival for strum timing.
446	
447	Detection thresholds are applied directly to raw pixel values (dark background is implicit zero, no settle/calibration phase).
448	
449	### Observed Game Colors (camera-captured BGR)
450	
451	Colors are highly saturated with negligible off-channel values:
452	
453	| Color  | B    | G    | R    | Notes |
454	|--------|------|------|------|-------|
455	| Red    | <10  | <10  | >100 | Almost completely red |
456	| Green  | <10  | >100 | <10  | Completely green |
457	| Blue   | >100 | ~67  | <10  | B dominant, G about 2/3 of B, low R |
458	| Yellow | <10  | ~100 | ~100 | Even mix of G and R, very low B |
459	| Orange | <10  | ~50  | >100 | R dominant, G about half of R, low B |
460	| White (fret bar) | ~160 | ~160 | ~160 | Equal channels at brightest, sat near 0 |
461	
462	The edge detector uses a color filter with saturation scaling `(max-min)/max` to reject white/gray fret bars regardless of camera white balance.
463	
464	### Parameters
465	
466	| Parameter | Default | Description |
467	|-----------|---------|-------------|
468	| `THRESHOLD` | 50 | Detection threshold (brightness for hold, color signal for edge) |
469	| `RELEASE_FRAC` | 60 | Release threshold as % of press threshold (hysteresis) |
470	| `PATCH_RADIUS` | 2 | Pixel averaging radius around sample point |
471	| `{COLOR}_X/Y` | varies | Hold sensor pixel coordinates per button |
472	| `{COLOR}_EX/EY` | varies | Edge sensor pixel coordinates per button |
473	
474	Camera selection lives in the always-on video subsystem, not the detector; there is no `DEVICE_ID` parameter here. Sensor markers are drawn through the `overlays()` hook, replacing the previous `SHOW_PREVIEW`/`/video` path.
475	
476	### Calibration
477	
478	Use `video_calibrate.py` to interactively mark sensor positions:
479	
480	```bash
481	# Full calibration (10 points: 5 hold + 5 edge)
482	python video_calibrate.py --device 0
483	
484	# Color sampling mode (inspect BGR values without calibrating)
485	python video_calibrate.py --sample
486	```

2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.10"

5	# ///
6	"""
7	Fretboard data-stream monitor.
8	
9	Reads the 12-byte frame emitted by data_stream.c:
10	    start (0x03) | green | red | yellow | blue | orange | end (0xFC)
11	where each colour is a little-endian uint16. Reports actual frame rate
12	and the latest values; flags framing errors.
13	
14	Usage:
15	    ./ds_monitor.py <port> [--baud 500000] [--expect-hz 240]
16	    uv run ds_monitor.py <port> ...
17	"""
18	import argparse
19	import struct
20	import sys
21	import time
22	
23	import serial  # pyserial
24	
25	START = 0x03
26	END = 0xFC
27	FRAME_FMT = "<BHHHHHB"
28	FRAME_LEN = struct.calcsize(FRAME_FMT)
29	assert FRAME_LEN == 12
30	
31	CHANNELS = ("green", "red", "yellow", "blue", "orange")
32	
33	
34	def find_frame(buf: bytearray) -> tuple[tuple[int, ...] | None, int]:
35	    """Return (values, dropped_bytes). values is None if no full frame yet.
36	       Skips bytes until a valid start+end pair is found; dropped_bytes
37	       counts misaligned bytes discarded during the search."""
38	    dropped = 0
39	    while len(buf) >= FRAME_LEN:
40	        if buf[0] != START or buf[FRAME_LEN - 1] != END:
41	            del buf[0]
42	            dropped += 1
43	            continue
44	        unpacked = struct.unpack(FRAME_FMT, bytes(buf[:FRAME_LEN]))
45	        del buf[:FRAME_LEN]
46	        return unpacked[1:6], dropped
47	    return None, dropped
48	
49	
50	def main() -> int:
51	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
52	    ap.add_argument("port", help="Serial port (e.g. /dev/tty.usbmodem...)")
53	    ap.add_argument("--baud", type=int, default=500_000)
54	    ap.add_argument("--expect-hz", type=float, default=240.0)
55	    ap.add_argument("--report-every", type=float, default=1.0,
56	                    help="Seconds between status lines")
57	    args = ap.parse_args()
58	
59	    ser = serial.Serial(args.port, args.baud, timeout=0.1)
60	    print(f"Listening on {args.port} @ {args.baud} baud, expecting {args.expect_hz} Hz")
61	
62	    buf = bytearray()
63	    frames = 0
64	    bytes_in = 0
65	    sync_drops = 0
66	    last_values: tuple[int, ...] | None = None
67	    t_start = time.monotonic()
68	    t_report = t_start
69	
70	    try:
71	        while True:
72	            chunk = ser.read(256)
73	            if chunk:
74	                bytes_in += len(chunk)
75	                buf.extend(chunk)
76	                while True:
77	                    values, dropped = find_frame(buf)
78	                    sync_drops += dropped
79	                    if values is None:
80	                        break
81	                    frames += 1
82	                    last_values = values
83	
84	            now = time.monotonic()
85	            if now - t_report >= args.report_every:
86	                dt = now - t_report
87	                hz = frames / dt
88	                t_report = now
89	                vals = (
90	                    " ".join(f"{c[0].upper()}{v:>4}" for c, v in zip(CHANNELS, last_values))
91	                    if last_values else "(no frames)"
92	                )
93	                drift = (hz - args.expect_hz) / args.expect_hz * 100 if args.expect_hz else 0
94	                print(f"{hz:6.1f} Hz ({drift:+5.1f}%)  bytes/s={bytes_in/dt:7.0f}  "
95	                      f"drops={sync_drops:3d}  buf={len(buf):3d}  {vals}")
96	                frames = 0
97	                bytes_in = 0
98	                sync_drops = 0
99	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
100	        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t_start
101	        print(f"\nStopped after {elapsed:.1f}s.")
102	    finally:
103	        ser.close()
104	    return 0
105	
106	
107	if __name__ == "__main__":
108	    sys.exit(main())

199	- Bugs found + fixed on hardware during cycle testing:
200	  - Disconnect left `connected=1` → `Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected` now clears
201	    `s_data_fd` immediately (not just on reader exit).
202	  - Reader tasks leaked their link slot when a re-armed server recycled their fd →
203	    readers now exit by **L2CAP handle** signalled from the CLOSE event, not by
204	    `read()` return.
205	  - **L2CAP slot exhaustion after ~4-5 reconnect cycles**: auto-re-arming servers on
206	    every disconnect leaked server slots (reconnect uses *client* connects, so the
207	    re-armed servers were never consumed). Fix: arm servers only per `pair` window,
208	    tear down on `stop`; no auto-re-arm.
209	- Open: device-initiated `reconnect` uses Basic L2CAP mode vs the Wii's ERTM (may
210	  misbehave) — reliable path is `pair`+SYNC.
211	
212	### 2026-06-12 — Phase 2b done: assigned Wiimote + status LED
213	
214	- `wiimote.c` report state machine (ported from rnconrad's `wm_reports`/handlers,
215	  explicit bytes, no bitfields): EEPROM read (`0x21`, calibration at 0x16/0x20,
216	  error for >0x16FF), status (`0x20`), ack (`0x22`), reporting-mode/LED/IR acks,
217	  and a static sender task streaming `0x30` every 15 ms. Register reads currently
218	  return an error (no extension yet → Phase 3).
219	- Wired into the L2CAP reader (`Wiimote_HandleRx` per frame, `Wiimote_NotifyFdClosed`
220	  on close). Added `status_led.c` driving GPIO13 (heartbeat/fast-blink/solid) since
221	  the Feather has no player LEDs; reflects `Wiimote_IsConnected/IsAssigned`.
222	- On hardware: full clean handshake (`0x17`×n, `0x11`, `0x15`, `0x12`, `0x13`/`0x1a`,
223	  `0x16` IR-register writes), Wii assigns a slot, **LED solid = assigned**. Turned
224	  off the verbose Bluedroid trace block in `sdkconfig.defaults` (needs `set-target`
225	  to re-apply) — monitor is now readable.
226	
227	### 2026-06-12 — Phase 2a: HID read path working
228	
229	- Added per-channel reader tasks (static `xTaskCreateStatic`) that `read()` the
230	  L2CAP fds from `ESP_BT_L2CAP_OPEN_EVT`. Gotcha: `esp_bt_l2cap`'s VFS `read()` is
231	  **non-blocking** — empty rx queue returns `0` (not EOF), peer-close returns `-1`
232	  (errno `EPIPE`). So poll on `0`, exit only on `<0` (first cut wrongly treated `0`
233	  as EOF and the reader exited instantly). No `select` support on this VFS.
234	- First output report from the Wii (data channel, PSM 0x13): `a2 17 00 00 17 70 00
235	  01` = report `0x17` Read Memory, EEPROM offset `0x001770`, size 1. The Wii then
236	  **blocks waiting for our `0x21` (Read Data) reply** — confirms the report
237	  responder is the gate to a live/assigned controller. → Phase 2b.
238	
239	### 2026-06-12 — Phase 1 complete: Wii pairs + opens HID channels
240	
241	- Custom SDP path works. Replaced esp_hidd with: `wiimote_sdp.c` building the exact
242	  Wiimote record via internal `SDP_CreateRecord`/`SDP_AddAttribute`/… (modeled on
243	  Bluedroid's own `HID_DevAddRecord`, Wiimote-exact values), + `esp_bt_l2cap`
244	  servers on PSM 0x11/0x13. Raised `CONFIG_BT_SDP_ATTR_LEN=512` /
245	  `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN=1024` (defaults exist; depend only on `BT_CLASSIC_ENABLED`).
246	- On red-SYNC: SDP accepted → legacy PIN pairing `auth OK` → both HID L2CAP
247	  channels open (CID 0x40 control / 0x41 interrupt, mtu 640) → Wii starts sending us
248	  HID data (`BTA_JvL2capRead`). Phase 1 success criterion met on hardware.
249	- Build/integration lessons (durable):
250	  - To call the internal SDP API, add bt internal include roots in CMake:
251	    `<bt>/common/include`, `<bt>/host/bluedroid/{stack,common,osi}/include`,
252	    `<bt>/host/bluedroid/api/include/api`. `bdroid_buildcfg.h` is behind
253	    `#ifdef HAS_BDROID_BUILDCFG` (not defined externally) so it's skipped.
254	  - `esp_bt_l2cap` data path is fd/VFS-based: must `esp_bt_l2cap_vfs_register()`
255	    (after INIT_EVT) BEFORE `esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv`, else `l2cap_malloc_slot
256	    unable to register fd` / NO_RESOURCE.

258	### 2026-06-12 — Phase 1 debugging: discovery solved, SDP rejected
259	
260	- esp_hidd HID-device first attempt — Wii initially saw nothing. Two fixes got it
261	  to connect: (a) the Wii's SYNC scan uses a *limited* inquiry → switched to
262	  `ESP_BT_LIMITED_DISCOVERABLE`; (b) `esp_hidd_dev_init` overrides the Class of
263	  Device → now set `0x002504` in the HIDD START handler (after init).
264	- **sdkconfig.defaults gotcha:** edits to `sdkconfig.defaults` do NOT apply once
265	  `sdkconfig` exists. `CONFIG_BT_SSP_ENABLED=n` + 8 MB flash silently didn't take
266	  effect until `idf.py set-target esp32` regenerated `sdkconfig`. Always regenerate
267	  (or menuconfig) after editing defaults.
268	- With legacy pairing active + verbose Bluedroid logs: Wii connects ACL → SDP
269	  (PSM 1) → reads our records → disconnects → ACL term `rsn 0x13`, never opening the
270	  HID PSMs. → Q1 resolved (see decision log). Pivoting to raw L2CAP + exact Wiimote
271	  SDP. Added a temporary verbose-BT-log block to `sdkconfig.defaults` (trim later).

Fix: ISC IRQ computes `slot = (frameIndex - 1 + N) % N` (driver increments before callback per drv_isc.c:47-50), passes `base + slot * frame_size` into the user callback, and video.c re-points HEO at that address with `XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(..., update=true)` — latches at next vsync. Also unblocks ring depth > 2 since each subscriber sees the genuinely-just-written buffer. |
88	| 2026-05-20 | `Video_SubscribeFrames` is multi-subscriber (max 4), each subscriber chooses its own queue depth + back-pressure policy | Need parallel video CV tasks (note detector + recording + future menu/score readers) on one capture pipeline. Static array of 4 `QueueHandle_t` slots; ISR fans out one `xQueueSendFromISR` per subscribed slot. Aligned-pointer slot reads/writes are atomic on Cortex-A5 so the IRQ can scan without locking; `taskENTER_CRITICAL` only needed in `Subscribe`/`Unsubscribe` to prevent two task-side writers racing on the same empty slot. Producer always uses `xQueueSendFromISR` (drop-on-full); consumer chooses queue depth — depth 1 = "newest only", deeper = "preserve every frame". |
89	| 2026-05-20 | All marvin-owned FreeRTOS objects use `xTaskCreateStatic` / `xQueueCreateStatic` / `xSemaphoreCreateMutexStatic`; FreeRTOS heap stays at heap_1 only because MCC code (XLCDC/MAXTOUCH/LEGATO/SYS_INPUT tasks, OSAL, Legato variable heap) needs it | Project rule is static-only memory allocation. MCC-generated code can't be made static without forking, so we keep `configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION = 1` for MCC and route all our own code through the static APIs. MCC reconfigured to enable `configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION = 1` and emit `vApplicationGetIdleTaskMemory` in `freertos_hooks.c`. Per-module `Static{Task,Queue,Semaphore}_t` plus stack/storage arrays at file scope. |
90	| 2026-05-20 | ISC framebuffer pool moved from `.region_cache_aligned` to `.region_nocache`; max capture cap dropped 1920×1080 → 1280×720 to fit | First CPU consumer of frame data (cv_marvin_v1) needed cache-coherent reads. Two paths considered: invalidate D-cache per frame in the ISR, or move the pool to the linker's already-defined uncached region. Nocache is simpler and bug-resistant — every reader sees DMA-fresh bytes without explicit maintenance. Trade is full-DDR-fetch on every read; fine for sparse 5×5 patch sampling, would matter for a full-frame scan. `ram_nocache` is 16 MB so the 4-buffer × 1080p pool (≈24 MB) had to shrink; capping at 720p (≈11 MB) matches our current TC358743 ceiling and leaves headroom. Reverting to 1080p later requires either growing `ram_nocache` in `ddram.ld` or going back to cached + manual invalidate. |
91	| 2026-05-20 | cv_marvin_v1 keeps detector internals (press_count, raw color distances) private; bus record stays canonical (`pressed[] / confidence / raw_value`) | Different detectors need different per-frame data, but downstream bus consumers (timing pipeline, recorder, fretboard link) only care about "is this fret pressed at frame N." Pushing detector-specific richness onto the bus would either grow the canonical record or force a tagged-union shape that complicates recording layout. Encapsulating internals in the detector module preserves the narrow bus and lets each detector evolve its own state independently. press_count specifically lives in a private `s_press_count[FRET_COUNT]` array; if the strum scheduler later wants it, expose via a getter or a second "detail" channel. Recording-format choice (custom packed binary vs nanopb vs CBOR) deferred to M5. |
92	| 2026-05-20 | cv_marvin_v1 sensor coords are in native capture-frame space, no 1920×1080 reference scaling | fret-tuner detect_video.py carries a 1920×1080 reference frame and scales coords at runtime — that frame size is what the Elgato HDMI-to-USB bridge produced, not a per-camera variable. Marvin uses the TC358743 (different bridge chip, same direct-pixel topology) and captures at the source's native resolution. The Wii is the primary production source at 480p60 = 720×480, so the static defaults are scaled from Python's 1920×1080 values by (3/8, 4/9) once at port time and stored in 720×480 space. Same-pixel-strike-line geometry as the Python detector — these are real coords, not placeholders. Calibration UI (M6) will refine them. |
93	| 2026-05-20 | Fretboard-link submit queue belongs to `fretboard_link`, not `timing_pipeline`; producers call `FretboardLink_Send(mask)` | Game menu control (spec §4.8) needs to drive the actuator without going through the chord-window scheduler — its inputs are "navigate menu, press start", not gameplay notes. If the queue lives in `timing_pipeline`, the controller has to either reach across modules or duplicate transport. Moving ownership down to `fretboard_link` makes timing_pipeline one of N producers; the menu controller and any manual-test path call the same `Send` API. Latest-wins (depth-1 + xQueueOverwrite) already gives the right behavior — newest submitter wins on the wire. **Mode-level arbitration** (which producer is allowed to submit when, e.g. timing-only during gameplay vs controller-only in menus) lives one layer up; the link stays dumb. |
94	| 2026-05-20 | M2 fretboard link split into three layers — `detector → timing_pipeline → fretboard_link` — with the timing FIFO living on marvin and a 1-byte bitmask wire format | (a) Three-layer split keeps each concern small: detector emits state, timing_pipeline owns chord-window + strum scheduling, fretboard_link owns the USB CDC byte channel. Each can be replaced independently (different detector, different actuator transport) without touching the others. (b) Timing FIFO on marvin, not fretboard: marvin already runs the canonical detector and the recording pipeline, so co-locating timing keeps a single source of truth and avoids re-deriving state on the actuator side. Spec §4.4. The fretboard-takeover fallback (spec §6) is a separate mode where marvin disables its pipeline and fretboard runs `fret_button.c` standalone — that's the high-availability path, not the steady-state. (c) 1-byte bitmask matches `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py` and `firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h` exactly (G/R/Y/B/O at bits 0..4, strum-down bit 5, strum-up bit 6) — no reason to invent a new framing while the protocol is this small. Latest-wins semantics on the marvin→fretboard queue (depth 1 + overwrite) so a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale chords. (d) **Actuator-latency compensation deferred until mechanical actuators arrive.** Today's actuator is direct GPIO assertion on the fretboard PCB — latency ≈ 0, so today's design is sound. Future paths considered: (1) marvin compensates by subtracting a fretboard-published latency from `assert_at`/`strum_at`; (2) fretboard compensates by accepting timestamped events and scheduling locally. Path 2 needs a richer wire format (event + abs-timestamp); path 1 keeps the byte protocol but pushes the timing math up. Pick when we know which actuator (voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid) we're driving. |
95	| 2026-05-20 | Game-state awareness & high-level game control is a marvin subsystem (spec §4.8). Distinct from the gameplay note-detection path: a video-frame consumer (not a detector) emits typed game-state events on `xGameStateQueue`, and a controller layer translates verbs ("start single-player song X") into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link | Want marvin to drive whole-session play, not just notes once gameplay starts. Game-state observation belongs on marvin because it's CV on the same captured frames. Separating its bus from `xDetectorStateQueue` keeps `detector_state_t` narrow per the 2026-05-20 multi-detector decision. Per-game catalog (menu graph + song list) is metadata kept on marvin. Default arbitration with timing pipeline: mutually exclusive — controller runs only outside `gameplay` state. Phasing: M9 observer-only, M10 control. Open: recognizer algorithm (Q10), arbitration boundary (Q11). |

109	- **`vApplicationStackOverflowHook` is a silent infinite-loop.** ([freertos_hooks.c:62-76](../default/src/config/default/freertos_hooks.c#L62-L76)) MCC's default is `taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS()` then `for (;;)`. An actual overflow is indistinguishable from any other freeze on hardware. Patch the hook to emit a `LOG_ERR` line naming the offending task before the spin (carefully — the stack is already corrupt, so the hook should avoid using locals or large stack frames). Already nearly bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. (HWM/RUNTIME records reach the host now post-2026-05-29 work, so we have *steady-state* stack visibility — but a real overflow still freezes silently.)

With the manual-control surface adding 8 buttons and frequent press/release events during menu nav, confirm `legato_config.h` `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` has headroom for typical event bursts. Watch for Legato heap-exhaustion symptoms (silent dropped events, widget redraw glitches) once the UI is exercised on hardware.

If a second Legato screen is ever added, `ManualInput_Bind` must re-run inside that screen's show path (or whichever screen owns the manual-control widgets). Not an issue today — flagged for whenever the operator UI grows beyond Screen0.

117	- **MCC-file modifications maintenance risk.** A from-scratch MCC regen on 2026-05-15 confirmed **four** local modifications get clobbered. The 2026-05-20 USB-host regen added a fifth. Re-apply after every regen:
118	
119	  1. **`plib_csi.c` — `CSI_Analog_Init` refactor.** MCC emits per-lane HS-RX init inline with three bugs: Lane 1 in the 2-lane branch is missing the bit-rate write, Lane 2's lane-select code is `0x24` instead of `0x64`, and the 4-lane else-if branch skips Lane 1 entirely. Replace with the `csi_phy_hs_rx_init(lane_code, bit_rate)` helper and call it for lanes 0/1/2/3 from a flat `if (nlanes >= …)` chain.
120	
121	  2. **`plib_xlcdc.c` `XLCDC_EnableClocks` — `PMC_PLL_ACR`.** Set to datasheet-optimal `0x12023010` for the LVDSPLL with our 24 MHz reference (in the `fIN ∈ [20 MHz, 32 MHz]` band). Specifically: `LOOP_FILTER=0x12, LOCK_THR=0x2, UTMIBG=1, UTMIVR=1, CONTROL=0x10`. MCC's default emits a different (less-optimal) analog config (`LOOP_FILTER=0x1B, LOCK_THR=0x4, no UTMI bits`). Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.
122	
123	  3. **`plib_csi2dc.c` `CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe` — `| CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1`.** Required by the RGB888-packed capture path: byte-stream packs 4 BGR pixels across 12 bytes per CSI-2 RMS spec (Table 49.27). Without it, capture writes wrong-format bytes and the display shows garbage. *(Earlier journal note claimed this was now MCC's default — incorrect; this regen confirmed MCC still emits without RMS_1.)*
124	
125	  4. **`drv_image_sensor.h` enum shim.** MCC's regen *deletes* this file when the image-sensor component is disabled. Restore the 30-line shim at `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/image_sensor/drv_image_sensor.h` defining `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RAW_BAYER…JPEG` and `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT…40_BIT` enums (numeric values must match the original — `drv_isc.c` derives `bits_per_pixel = 4 - inputBits`). Without it, `drv_isc.c` and `configuration.h` won't compile.
126	
127	  5. **`initialization.c` `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` — per-pin VBUS calls.** **(Obsolete on the SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid — no USB host; the VBUS enables were removed from `app.c` on 2026-06-08.)** MCC emits a single `VBUS_AH_*_Set/Clear()` call expecting one pin named `VBUS_AH`, but our config has VBUS on two pins (PC27 + PC31, one per USB port). The pin-macro generator produces `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_*` and `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_*` separately and no unified wrapper, so the MCC-emitted code fails to compile. Replace lines 162-163 (Set branch) and 169-170 (Clear branch) with explicit calls to both per-pin macros — `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set(); VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set();` and the matching Clear pair. The MCC comment in the function ("name it to 'VBUS_AH'") acknowledges the single-pin assumption.
128	
129	  6. **`initialization.c` `SYS_Initialize` — peripheral init order.** **(Hybrid board: the peripheral is now `FLEXCOM8_TWI_Initialize` (not FLEXCOM6) and there's no USB-host regen, but the MMU/AIC-before-peripherals concern still stands — verified intact on 2026-06-08: MMU/AIC run before TC0/FLEXCOM2/FLEXCOM8/XLCDC.)** The USB-host MCC regen (2026-05-20) reordered SYS_Initialize so that `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize` run *before* `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize`. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.
130	
131	  7. **`usb_host_cdc.c` — accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0` in CDC ACM Communications-interface match.** **(Obsolete on the SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid — the USB host stack was removed in `598d370`; this patch only matters on a host-capable board.)** Two checks (single-interface path ~line 677, IAD path ~line 798) currently require `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG-style USB-to-UART bridges (the on-board PIC/AVR debugger CDC, common across Microchip dev boards — including the fretboard board this project uses) declare the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol = USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC` (`0x00`). Without this patch the host CDC driver accepts the IAD via the TPL match (TPL ignores subclass/protocol) but rejects the comm interface inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign`, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to `STATE_ERROR`, and the app-level attach handler never fires. Patch: extend each check to `(... == AT_V250 || ... == NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. Two one-line OR additions. Re-apply after every USB-host MCC regen.
132	
133	  8. **`FreeRTOSConfig.h` — `portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS` / `portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE` macros + 64-bit counter type.** With `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS = 1` (set via `FREERTOS_GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` MCC symbol), FreeRTOS expects the application to provide a free-running counter. MCC's FreeRTOS Harmony component does not expose a knob for an app-specific counter source. Append at the end of `FreeRTOSConfig.h` (just before `#endif`):
134	     ```c
135	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
136	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
137	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
138	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
139	     ```
140	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.
141	
142	  9. **`drv_usb_udphs_device.c` — multi-IRP DMA arming in completion ISRs.** Stock UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch (line 1604+); IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in (line 2273-2284 of patched file via `iterator->next = irp_t`) but never get armed for transmission. `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after firing the callback but does not re-program DMA hardware. Result: only one IRP per "queue idle" sequence ever transmits — the rest sit `STATUS_PENDING` forever.
143	
144	      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). Then add a call after the queue advance in **two** places:
145	
146	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
147	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
148	
149	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. Helper carries the same cache-clean and DMA-program shape as the inline original, including the `__DSB(); __ISB();` barriers and the `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr` for the IRP data buffer.
150	
151	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.
152	
153	  10. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. Re-apply after every maXTouch MCC regen.

Easy/Medium/Hard place notes higher up the highway with longer travel time, so the same 220 ms may strike too early. 171	- **T1S link transport — direction, not yet built.** Plan to replace the FLEXCOM2 USART fretboard link with **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** (LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY each end). System spec §6 + [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md). marvin runs **bare-metal**, so it gets *no free netdev* — it needs its own OA TC6 SPI driver. Plan: a single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared with fretboard (Cortex-A5 + Cortex-M0+). `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` stays the public API; only the transport beneath it swaps (SPI + TC6 chunk protocol + a 14-byte L2 header wrapping the existing 17-byte/1-byte frames). marvin resources are not a concern. PoDL is dumb (fixed voltage, no SCCP) and transparent to the MCU. Decide topology (PLCA vs p2p), ethertype/MACs, and UART-fallback-during-bring-up before code lands.

Per-frame luma normalization handles gain/offset. 146	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.

151	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.
152	
153	  10. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. Re-apply after every maXTouch MCC regen.

141	## Hardware cost note (SAM9X75 port target)
142	
143	ARM926EJ-S, ARMv5TE, single core, up to 800 MHz, no SIMD. The classifier is **memory-bound,
144	not compute-bound** — the dominant cost is reading frame pixels from the uncached DDR
145	framebuffer (~50–150 MB/s sequential; ~50–150 ns per strided single access). Compute
146	(per-region integer sums + an L1 distance over 13 templates ≈ a couple thousand byte ops) is
147	microseconds.
148	
149	- Dense (every pixel, 720×480×3 ≈ 1.04 MB): **~7–20 ms**.
150	- Subsampled lattice (default 12×8 × 5×5 = 2400 reads): **~0.1–0.4 ms**.
151	
152	Either is far from "seconds"; the observer needs only a few Hz for menu navigation, so the
153	subsampled path costs <1% CPU at 5–10 Hz.

Replace with the `csi_phy_hs_rx_init(lane_code, bit_rate)` helper and call it for lanes 0/1/2/3 from a flat `if (nlanes >= …)` chain.
120	
121	  2. **`plib_xlcdc.c` `XLCDC_EnableClocks` — `PMC_PLL_ACR`.** Set to datasheet-optimal `0x12023010` for the LVDSPLL with our 24 MHz reference (in the `fIN ∈ [20 MHz, 32 MHz]` band). Specifically: `LOOP_FILTER=0x12, LOCK_THR=0x2, UTMIBG=1, UTMIVR=1, CONTROL=0x10`. MCC's default emits a different (less-optimal) analog config (`LOOP_FILTER=0x1B, LOCK_THR=0x4, no UTMI bits`). Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.
122	
123	  3. **`plib_csi2dc.c` `CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe` — `| CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1`.** Required by the RGB888-packed capture path: byte-stream packs 4 BGR pixels across 12 bytes per CSI-2 RMS spec (Table 49.27). Without it, capture writes wrong-format bytes and the display shows garbage. *(Earlier journal note claimed this was now MCC's default — incorrect; this regen confirmed MCC still emits without RMS_1.)*
124	
125	  4. **`drv_image_sensor.h` enum shim.** MCC's regen *deletes* this file when the image-sensor component is disabled. Restore the 30-line shim at `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/image_sensor/drv_image_sensor.h` defining `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RAW_BAYER…JPEG` and `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT…40_BIT` enums (numeric values must match the original — `drv_isc.c` derives `bits_per_pixel = 4 - inputBits`). Without it, `drv_isc.c` and `configuration.h` won't compile.
126	
127	  5. **`initialization.c` `SYS_Initialize` — peripheral init order.** **(Hybrid board: the peripheral is now `FLEXCOM8_TWI_Initialize` (not FLEXCOM6) and there's no USB-host regen, but the MMU/AIC-before-peripherals concern still stands — verified intact on 2026-06-08: MMU/AIC run before TC0/FLEXCOM2/FLEXCOM8/XLCDC.)** The USB-host MCC regen (2026-05-20) reordered SYS_Initialize so that `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize` run *before* `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize`. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.

129	  6. **`FreeRTOSConfig.h` — `portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS` / `portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE` macros + 64-bit counter type.** With `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS = 1` (set via `FREERTOS_GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` MCC symbol), FreeRTOS expects the application to provide a free-running counter. MCC's FreeRTOS Harmony component does not expose a knob for an app-specific counter source. Append at the end of `FreeRTOSConfig.h` (just before `#endif`):
130	     ```c
131	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
132	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
133	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
134	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
135	     ```
136	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.

Result: only one IRP per "queue idle" sequence ever transmits — the rest sit `STATUS_PENDING` forever.

140	      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). 141	
142	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
143	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
144	
145	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. Helper carries the same cache-clean and DMA-program shape as the inline original, including the `__DSB(); __ISB();` barriers and the `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr` for the IRP data buffer.
146	
147	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.

149	  8. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. 30	/* RX notification threshold: wake the parse task once a full frame's worth of
31	 * bytes has landed in the FLEXCOM1 RX ring. The ring (sized in MCC) keeps
32	 * receiving continuously, so there is no per-read re-arm gap to lose bytes

34	#define FBL_RX_THRESHOLD        DS_FRAME_LEN
35	
36	/* Idle heartbeat: re-send last mask if the timing pipeline goes quiet, so
37	 * a stalled detector or paused game can't leave a stale frets-active
38	 * pattern stuck on the wire. 50 ms is well below human-perceptible. */
39	#define FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS        50u
40	
41	/* Bound the RX wait so a missed notification can't wedge the parser; the

43	#define FBL_RX_WAIT_MS          100u

45	/* Link runs at 500 000 baud, 8N1 — configured by the MCC FLEXCOM1 USART

50	static StaticQueue_t s_cmd_queue_buf;
51	static uint8_t       s_cmd_queue_storage[FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(uint8_t)];
52	
53	static StackType_t   s_task_stack[FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
54	static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;

56	static StackType_t   s_rx_task_stack[FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS];

59	/* Given from the FLEXCOM1 read callback (ISR) when the RX ring crosses the
60	 * frame threshold; woken thread drains and parses. */
61	static SemaphoreHandle_t s_rx_notify;
62	static StaticSemaphore_t s_rx_notify_buf;
63	
64	/* A UART has no enumeration step — the link is up once Initialize has armed
65	 * the peripheral. Kept so producers and the heartbeat path can gate sends. */
66	static volatile bool s_link_up;
67	
68	/* Asserted-mask snapshot: most recent byte accepted into the FLEXCOM1 TX ring.
69	 * Producer-side intent goes out on the same wire byte but may be overwritten
70	 * before it transmits if Send is called faster than the link services. The
71	 * PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record carries both. */
72	static volatile uint8_t  s_last_sent_byte;
73	
74	/* Last send result + timestamp, snapshotted into the ACTUATOR record so the
75	 * host can read Send-to-ack latency. A ring-buffer Write copies the byte and
76	 * returns immediately, so "ack" is the enqueue instant. */
77	static volatile int32_t  s_last_ack_result;
78	static volatile uint64_t s_last_ack_ts_counter;

80	static void rx_event_handler(FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT event, uintptr_t context)
81	{
82	    (void)context;
83	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
84	
85	    switch (event)
86	    {
87	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_THRESHOLD_REACHED:
88	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_BUFFER_FULL:
89	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
90	            break;
91	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_ERROR:
92	            /* Consume + clear the error status; the resync parser recovers
93	             * frame alignment on the next valid start/end pair. */
94	            (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ErrorGet();
95	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
96	            break;
97	        default:
98	            break;
99	    }
100	
101	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
102	}
103	
104	static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
105	{
106	    if (!s_link_up) { return false; }
107	
108	    uint8_t tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
109	
110	    /* Ring-buffer Write copies the byte into the TX ring and returns the
111	     * count accepted; for a single byte this only fails if the TX ring is
112	     * full, which shouldn't happen at command rates. */
113	    if (FLEXCOM1_USART_Write(&tx_byte, 1u) != 1u)
114	    {
115	        LOG_WARN("FBL: TX ring full, byte dropped\r\n");
116	        return false;
117	    }
118	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND, 0u, (uint32_t)tx_byte);
119	
120	    s_last_sent_byte      = tx_byte;
121	    s_last_ack_result     = 0;
122	    s_last_ack_ts_counter = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
123	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE, 0u, 0u);
124	    return true;
125	}
126	
127	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
128	{
129	    (void)param;
130	
131	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started (FLEXCOM1)\r\n");
132	
133	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
134	
135	    for (;;)
136	    {
137	        uint8_t mask;
138	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
139	        {
140	            last_mask = mask;
141	        }
142	        else
143	        {
144	            mask = last_mask;
145	        }
146	
147	        (void)send_one_byte(mask);
148	    }
149	}
150	
151	/* Drain the FLEXCOM1 RX ring and emit one PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW per parsed
152	 * 17-byte frame. Resync logic mirrors tools/ds_monitor.py: a frame is valid
153	 * only when buf[0]==0x03 AND buf[16]==0xFC; otherwise drop the leading byte
154	 * and retry alignment. The FSM-free buffered approach is easier to reason
155	 * about than a state machine and the frame is short. */
156	static void fretboard_rx_task(void *param)
157	{
158	    (void)param;
159	
160	    uint8_t  frame[DS_FRAME_LEN];
161	    size_t   filled = 0u;
162	    uint32_t parsed = 0u;
163	    uint32_t skipped_bytes = 0u;
164	
165	    for (;;)
166	    {
167	        if (FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
168	        {
169	            (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_rx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_RX_WAIT_MS));
170	            continue;
171	        }
172	
173	        size_t want = DS_FRAME_LEN - filled;
174	        size_t got  = FLEXCOM1_USART_Read(&frame[filled], want);
175	        if (got == 0u) { continue; }
176	        filled += got;
177	        if (filled < DS_FRAME_LEN) { continue; }
178	
179	        if (frame[0] != DS_START_BYTE || frame[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] != DS_END_BYTE)
180	        {
181	            /* Misaligned: drop one byte and shift, then loop to refill. */
182	            memmove(&frame[0], &frame[1], DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u);
183	            filled = DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u;
184	            skipped_bytes++;
185	            continue;
186	        }
187	
188	        uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT];
189	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
190	        {
191	            adc[i] = (uint16_t)frame[1u + i * 2u]
192	                   | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)frame[2u + i * 2u] << 8);
193	        }
194	
195	        /* seq: u32 LE at bytes 11-14, applied_mask: u8 at byte 15. */
196	        uint32_t fb_seq = (uint32_t)frame[11]
197	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[12] << 8)
198	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[13] << 16)
199	                        | ((uint32_t)frame[14] << 24);
200	        uint8_t  applied_mask = frame[15];
201	
202	        Video_FrameInfo info;
203	        Video_GetFrameInfo(&info);
204	        PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(adc, info.frame_count, fb_seq, applied_mask);
205	
206	        parsed++;
207	        if (parsed == 1u || (parsed % 240u) == 0u)
208	        {
209	            LOG_DEBUG("FBL: rx parsed=%u skipped=%u G=%u R=%u Y=%u B=%u O=%u\r\n",
210	                      (unsigned)parsed, (unsigned)skipped_bytes,
211	                      (unsigned)adc[0], (unsigned)adc[1], (unsigned)adc[2],
212	                      (unsigned)adc[3], (unsigned)adc[4]);
213	        }
214	
215	        filled = 0u;
216	    }
217	}

219	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
220	{
221	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
222	                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
223	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
224	                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
225	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
226	
227	    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
228	    configASSERT(s_rx_notify != NULL);
229	
230	    /* Arm continuous RX: the ring fills from the FLEXCOM1 ISR; persistent
231	     * threshold notification wakes fretboard_rx_task each time a frame's
232	     * worth of bytes is available. */
233	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
234	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadThresholdSet(FBL_RX_THRESHOLD);
235	    (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);
236	
237	    s_link_up = true;
238	
239	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
240	                                       "FretLink",
241	                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
242	                                       NULL,
243	                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
244	                                       s_task_stack,
245	                                       &s_task_tcb);
246	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);
247	
248	    TaskHandle_t hr = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_rx_task,
249	                                        "FretRx",
250	                                        FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
251	                                        NULL,
252	                                        FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
253	                                        s_rx_task_stack,
254	                                        &s_rx_task_tcb);
255	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX, hr);
256	}
257	
258	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
259	{
260	    return s_link_up;
261	}
262	
263	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
264	{
265	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
266	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
267	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
268	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled write from accumulating
269	     * stale chord state. */
270	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
271	
272	    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
273	    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
274	    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }
275	
276	    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
277	                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
278	}

25	 * not the ISR, so it may be slower than the 240 Hz sample rate). Distinct length
26	 * (21 B) from the 17 B marvin frame; the standalone host parser keys on it. */
27	typedef struct __attribute__((packed)) {
28	    uint8_t  start;
29	    uint16_t green;
30	    uint16_t red;
31	    uint16_t yellow;
32	    uint16_t blue;
33	    uint16_t orange;
34	    uint32_t sample_seq;
35	    uint32_t infer_count;   /* total model inferences so far (main loop) */
36	    uint8_t  applied_mask;
37	    uint8_t  end;
38	} ds_model_frame_t;
39	
40	_Static_assert(sizeof(ds_model_frame_t) == 21, "model frame must be 21 bytes");
41	
42	static uint32_t s_sample_seq;
43	
44	void data_stream_init(void)
45	{
46	}
47	
48	bool data_stream_send(void)
49	{
50	    /* Advance per tick (before the buffer check) so a dropped send leaves a
51	     * gap in the transmitted sequence the host can detect. */
52	    uint32_t seq = s_sample_seq++;
53	
54	    if (SERCOM1_USART_WriteFreeBufferCountGet() < sizeof(ds_frame_t))
55	        return false;
56	
57	    ds_frame_t frame = {
58	        .start          = DS_START_BYTE,
59	        .green          = fret_scan_result(FRET_GREEN),
60	        .red            = fret_scan_result(FRET_RED),
61	        .yellow         = fret_scan_result(FRET_YELLOW),
62	        .blue           = fret_scan_result(FRET_BLUE),
63	        .orange         = fret_scan_result(FRET_ORANGE),
64	        .sample_seq     = seq,
65	        .applied_mask   = cmd_receive_current_mask(),
66	        .end            = DS_END_BYTE,
67	    };
68	
69	    SERCOM1_USART_Write((uint8_t *)&frame, sizeof(frame));
70	    return true;
71	}
72	
73	bool data_stream_send_model(uint32_t infer_count)
74	{
75	    uint32_t seq = s_sample_seq++;
76	
77	    if (SERCOM1_USART_WriteFreeBufferCountGet() < sizeof(ds_model_frame_t))
78	        return false;
79	
80	    ds_model_frame_t frame = {
81	        .start          = DS_START_BYTE,
82	        .green          = fret_scan_result(FRET_GREEN),
83	        .red            = fret_scan_result(FRET_RED),
84	        .yellow         = fret_scan_result(FRET_YELLOW),
85	        .blue           = fret_scan_result(FRET_BLUE),
86	        .orange         = fret_scan_result(FRET_ORANGE),
87	        .sample_seq     = seq,
88	        .infer_count    = infer_count,
89	        .applied_mask   = cmd_receive_current_mask(),
90	        .end            = DS_END_BYTE,
91	    };
92	
93	    SERCOM1_USART_Write((uint8_t *)&frame, sizeof(frame));
94	    return true;
95	}

19	 * lit while enabled. Boots disabled: outputs released, LED off, until pressed.
