21	 * Board polarity: the MCC pin config (PB03 pull-up, PB02 boots high) implies
22	 * SW0 and LED0 are both active-low. If at power-up the model auto-enables and
23	 * thrashes before you touch SW0, the pin idles low — set SW0_ACTIVE_LOW to 0.
24	 * If LED0 is inverted, set LED0_ACTIVE_LOW to 0. */
25	#define SW0_ACTIVE_LOW          1
26	#define LED0_ACTIVE_LOW         1
27	#define ENABLE_DEBOUNCE_TICKS   12u   /* ~50 ms at 240 Hz */
28	
29	#if SW0_ACTIVE_LOW
30	#define SW0_PRESSED()   (SW0_Get() == 0U)
31	#else
32	#define SW0_PRESSED()   (SW0_Get() != 0U)
33	#endif
34	#if LED0_ACTIVE_LOW
35	#define LED0_ON()       LED0_Clear()
36	#define LED0_OFF()      LED0_Set()
37	#else
38	#define LED0_ON()       LED0_Set()
39	#define LED0_OFF()      LED0_Clear()
40	#endif
41	
42	/* Latest command from the (main-loop) inference, applied by the TC0 ISR. A
43	 * single byte, so reads/writes are atomic on the M0+ — inference runs outside
44	 * the ISR so it can't starve the 240 Hz sampling or the serial TX interrupt. */
45	static volatile uint8_t s_latest_cmd;
46	
47	/* Total inferences run in the main loop; streamed each tick so the host can
48	 * measure the real inference rate (vs the 240 Hz sample rate). 32-bit aligned
49	 * → atomic single-word access on the M0+. */
50	static volatile uint32_t s_infer_count;
51	
52	static bool    s_model_enabled;
53	static bool    s_sw_pressed;          /* debounced button state */
54	static uint8_t s_sw_stable;           /* consecutive reads pushing toward a flip */
55	
56	#if MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
57	/* SPSC sample queue: the ISR pushes one scan/tick, the main loop steps the
58	 * stateful streaming model once per sample (it must consume every sample in
59	 * order). Stays near-empty while inference keeps up (>240 Hz). */
60	static volatile uint16_t s_adc_q[ADC_Q_LEN][FRET_COUNT];
61	static volatile uint16_t s_q_wr;      /* ISR-advanced write index */
62	static volatile uint16_t s_q_rd;      /* main-advanced read index */
63	#endif
64	
65	static bool model_control_enabled(void)
66	{
67	    bool raw = SW0_PRESSED();
68	    if (raw == s_sw_pressed)
69	    {
70	        s_sw_stable = 0u;
71	    }
72	    else if (++s_sw_stable >= ENABLE_DEBOUNCE_TICKS)
73	    {
74	        s_sw_pressed = raw;
75	        s_sw_stable = 0u;
76	        if (s_sw_pressed)             /* toggle on a confirmed press edge */
77	        {
78	            s_model_enabled = !s_model_enabled;
79	            if (s_model_enabled) { LED0_ON(); } else { LED0_OFF(); }
80	        }
81	    }
82	    return s_model_enabled;
83	}
84	#endif
85	
86	void Callback_TC0 (TC_TIMER_STATUS status, uintptr_t context)
87	{
88	    fret_scan_all();
89	
90	#if FRETBOARD_MODE == MODEL_DRIVEN
91	#if MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
92	    uint16_t wi = s_q_wr;
93	    for (int c = 0; c < FRET_COUNT; c++)
94	    {
95	        s_adc_q[wi % ADC_Q_LEN][c] = fret_scan_result((fret_channel_t)c);
96	    }
97	    s_q_wr = (uint16_t)(wi + 1u);   /* publish the sample to the main loop */
98	#else
99	    uint16_t scan[FRET_COUNT] = {
100	        fret_scan_result(FRET_GREEN),
101	        fret_scan_result(FRET_RED),
102	        fret_scan_result(FRET_YELLOW),
103	        fret_scan_result(FRET_BLUE),
104	        fret_scan_result(FRET_ORANGE),
105	    };
106	    model_infer_push(scan);   /* sample the window at a clean 240 Hz */
107	#endif
108	    /* Apply the most recent inference result; the heavy inference runs in the
109	     * main loop, not here, so this ISR stays short. */
110	    cmd_receive_apply_mask(model_control_enabled() ? s_latest_cmd : 0u);
111	    data_stream_send_model(s_infer_count);   /* carries applied_mask + inference count */
112	#else
113	    data_stream_send();
114	    cmd_receive_update();
115	#endif
116	}
117	
118	int main(void)
119	{
120	    SYS_Initialize(NULL);
121	
122	    fret_scan_init();
123	    cmd_receive_init();
124	    data_stream_init();
125	#if FRETBOARD_MODE == MODEL_DRIVEN
126	#if MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
127	    model_infer_stream_init();
128	#else
129	    model_infer_init();
130	#endif
131	    LED0_OFF();   /* boot disabled: LED off */
132	#endif
133	
134	    TC0_TimerCallbackRegister( Callback_TC0, NULL );
135	    TC0_TimerStart();
136	
137	    while (true) {
138	#if FRETBOARD_MODE == MODEL_DRIVEN
139	#if MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
140	        /* Drain the sample queue: one streaming step per sample, in order. */
141	        while (s_q_rd != s_q_wr)
142	        {
143	            uint16_t ri = s_q_rd;
144	            uint16_t s[FRET_COUNT];
145	            for (int c = 0; c < FRET_COUNT; c++) { s[c] = s_adc_q[ri % ADC_Q_LEN][c]; }
146	            s_latest_cmd = model_infer_stream_step(s);
147	            s_q_rd = (uint16_t)(ri + 1u);
148	            s_infer_count++;
149	        }
150	#else
151	        /* Best-effort recompute inference, decoupled from the 240 Hz sampling/apply
152	         * in the ISR. Publishes the latest command for the ISR to apply. */
153	        s_latest_cmd = model_infer_run();
154	        s_infer_count++;
155	#endif
156	#endif
157	    }
158	
159	    return EXIT_FAILURE;
160	}

73	        }
74	    }

12	
13	/* Split [0, extent) into `n` contiguous spans; edge(i) = round(i*extent/n). */
14	static int gp_edge(int i, int extent, int n)
15	{
16	    return (int)lround((double)i * (double)extent / (double)n);
17	}
18	
19	/* j-th of `n` sample coordinates centred in their sub-cell of [lo, hi). */
20	static int gp_lattice(int j, int lo, int hi, int n)
21	{
22	    int c = (int)((double)lo + (((double)j + 0.5) / (double)n) * (double)(hi - lo));
23	    if (c < lo)      { c = lo; }
24	    if (c > hi - 1)  { c = hi - 1; }
25	    return c;
26	}
27	
28	/* Mean BGR over the GP_FP_SAMPLES × GP_FP_SAMPLES lattice of a region. */
29	static void gp_region_mean(const uint8_t *frame, int w,
30	                           int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1, float out[3])
31	{
32	    uint32_t sb = 0u, sg = 0u, sr = 0u;
33	    int n = GP_FP_SAMPLES;
34	    for (int jy = 0; jy < n; jy++)
35	    {
36	        int y = gp_lattice(jy, y0, y1, n);
37	        const uint8_t *row = frame + (uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)w * GP_BPP;
38	        for (int jx = 0; jx < n; jx++)
39	        {
40	            int x = gp_lattice(jx, x0, x1, n);
41	            const uint8_t *p = row + (uint32_t)x * GP_BPP;
42	            sb += p[0];
43	            sg += p[1];
44	            sr += p[2];
45	        }
46	    }
47	    float cnt = (float)(n * n);
48	    out[0] = (float)sb / cnt;
49	    out[1] = (float)sg / cnt;
50	    out[2] = (float)sr / cnt;
51	}
52	
53	/* Fingerprint scratch in normalized float space, reduced to uint8. Static — the
54	 * single observer task is the only caller (see header). */
55	static float s_fp_f[GP_FP_LEN];

57	int gp_fingerprint(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, uint8_t *out)
58	{

60	
61	    int idx = 0;
62	    for (int r = 0; r < GP_FP_ROWS; r++)
63	    {
64	        int y0 = gp_edge(r, GP_CANON_H, GP_FP_ROWS);
65	        int y1 = gp_edge(r + 1, GP_CANON_H, GP_FP_ROWS);
66	        for (int c = 0; c < GP_FP_COLS; c++)
67	        {
68	            int x0 = gp_edge(c, GP_CANON_W, GP_FP_COLS);
69	            int x1 = gp_edge(c + 1, GP_CANON_W, GP_FP_COLS);
70	            float bgr[3];
71	            gp_region_mean(frame, width, x0, y0, x1, y1, bgr);
72	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[0];
73	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[1];
74	            s_fp_f[idx++] = bgr[2];
75	        }
76	    }
77

79	    double sum = 0.0;
80	    for (int i = 0; i < GP_FP_LEN; i++) { sum += s_fp_f[i]; }

Let me verify the frame layout from the spec against the code. The 17-byte frame should be:
- byte 0: 0x03 (start)
- bytes 1-10: G, R, Y, B, O (5 uint16_t LE = 10 bytes)
- bytes 11-14: sample_seq (uint32 LE = 4 bytes)
- byte 15: applied_mask (uint8)
- byte 16: 0xFC (end)

10	/* Game-state observer — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.8 (M9).
11	 *
12	 * A video-frame consumer (not a detector): it classifies which GH3 screen the
13	 * captured frame shows and publishes typed game_state_t events on its own bus
14	 * (xGameStateQueue), kept separate from the detector-state bus per the §4.2
15	 * multi-detector decision. The recognizer data (region grid, per-class
16	 * centroids, thresholds) is the host-proven metadata frozen into
17	 * game/gameplay_metadata.h by `gameplay export-c`.
18	 *
19	 * Phase 1 (this module): screen classification only. Selection/song readers
20	 * (Phase 2) and the navigator/controller (Phase 3, M10) build on this. */
21	
22	typedef struct
23	{
24	    uint32_t frame_epoch;   /* master sync token, = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count */
25	    uint64_t timestamp_us;  /* monotonic, marvin-local */
26	    uint8_t  screen;        /* GP_SCREEN_* index, or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN */
27	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
28	    int32_t  best_dist;     /* L1 to the nearest centroid */
29	    int32_t  margin;        /* second-best − best (confidence) */
30	    int16_t  selection;     /* static-list cell, song-template index, or -1 (none) */
31	} game_state_t;
32	
33	/* Brings up the game-state bus queue and the observer task. The observer
34	 * subscribes to the video frame queue from inside its task, so call this after
35	 * Video_Initialize. Observation starts disabled; call SetObserveEnabled(true)
36	 * to begin publishing (spec §6 game_observe_enable). */
37	void GameplayEngine_Initialize(void);
38	
39	/* Game-state event bus. Consumers (operator UI, the controller at M10) read
40	 * here. Returns NULL until GameplayEngine_Initialize has run. */
41	QueueHandle_t GameplayEngine_BusQueue(void);
42	
43	/* Observation toggle. When off the task still drains frames (so the video
44	 * queue doesn't back up) but classifies nothing and emits no events. */
45	void GameplayEngine_SetObserveEnabled(bool on);
46	bool GameplayEngine_ObserveEnabled(void);
47	
48	/* Force the observer to run on the next captured frame, bypassing the ~5 Hz
49	 * background rate limit. Intended for closed-loop control (M10): read the result
50	 * of an actuator command promptly instead of waiting for the next background
51	 * tick. One-shot (cleared once consumed); thread-safe (single volatile flag).
52	 *
53	 * NOTE: don't trigger this the instant after sending the command — GH3 menus

55	 * screen). The caller should let the screen settle first (a delay, and/or poll
56	 * until the expected screen appears with a timeout) rather than trust a single
57	 * immediate read. That settle policy lives in the controller (M10). */

11	 * Inference implementation (MODEL_DRIVEN only):
12	 *   0 = recompute (model_infer.c)        — works at any trained window; ~93 Hz
13	 *       at 16ch (re-runs the receptive field each tick).
14	 *   1 = streaming  (model_infer_stream.c) — caches per-layer columns, locks to
15	 *       the 240 Hz sample rate; REQUIRES a model trained at window >= the
16	 *       receptive field (85). (default)
17	 *
18	 * Both model_infer.c and model_infer_stream.c can stay in the project: each
19	 * guards its body on MODEL_INFER_STREAMING, so only the active one compiles its
20	 * static buffers (the inactive TU is empty — no .bss). Flip the mode here (or
21	 * with -D) — no add/remove of source files.
22	 */
23	
24	#define MARVIN_DRIVEN 0
25	#define MODEL_DRIVEN  1
26	#ifndef FRETBOARD_MODE
27	#define FRETBOARD_MODE MODEL_DRIVEN
28	#endif
29	
30	#ifndef MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
31	#define MODEL_INFER_STREAMING 1
32	#endif
33	
34	#endif /* FRETBOARD_CONFIG_H */

34:A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over a FLEXCOM2 UART link, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
41:| Display path (DDR → XLCDC HEO → LVDSC → panel) | ✅ working, pillarboxed/letterboxed, per-frame pointer swap. See [`display_path.md`](display_path.md). |

135:| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
143:1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144:2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
149:7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150:8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
156:| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157:| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
159:| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
175:| **fretboard board** (PIC32CM6408PL10048) | Sensor + actuator MCU | FLEXCOM1 USART (marvin PA28 TX / PA29 RX ↔ fretboard SERCOM1 PB01 RX / PB00 TX, 500 000 Bd 8N1, ring-buffer mode). |
186:| XLCDC + LVDSC | ✅ in use | HEO layer, RGB\_888\_PACKED, per-frame pointer swap, pillarbox/letterbox. |
189:| FLEXCOM1 (USART) | ✅ in use | Fretboard link — 500 000 Bd 8N1, ring-buffer mode (§4.3). |
207:Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
211:- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
224:This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
230:- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
239:    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
251:Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
258:- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
266:- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
275:Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)
278:- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
300:- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
302:**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
308:1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
310:3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.

- byte 0: start (uint8)
- bytes 1-2: green (uint16 LE)
- bytes 3-4: red (uint16 LE)
- bytes 5-6: yellow (uint16 LE)
- bytes 7-8: blue (uint16 LE)

- bytes 11-14: sample_seq (uint32 LE)
- byte 15: applied_mask (uint8)
- byte 16: end (uint8)

- frame[1] + (frame[2] << 8) for green (bytes 1-2) ✓
- frame[11] + (frame[12]<<8) + (frame[13]<<16) + (frame[14]<<24) for sample_seq ✓
- frame[15] for applied_mask ✓

1	# fauxmote — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for fauxmote. Newest entries at the top. For *what fauxmote is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, milestones), read [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Current focus
8	
9	**Phase 1 DONE — the Wii pairs with fauxmote and opens both HID channels.** Custom
10	Wiimote SDP record (built via Bluedroid's internal `SDP_*` API in `wiimote_sdp.c`,
11	with SDP buffers raised to 512/1024) + raw `esp_bt_l2cap` servers on PSM 0x11/0x13.
12	On a red-SYNC press the Wii: accepts our SDP, completes legacy PIN pairing
13	(`auth OK`), and opens both HID L2CAP channels (control CID 0x40 / interrupt CID 0x41,
14	both `mtu 640`), then starts sending us data. Wii BD_ADDR `00:17:ab:07:2c:21`.
15	
16	**Phase 2 DONE — the Wii fully initializes fauxmote as an assigned Wiimote.**
17	`wiimote.c` answers the Wii's output reports (`0x17` read→`0x21`, `0x15`→`0x20`
18	status, `0x16` write→`0x22` ack, `0x11` LEDs, `0x12` reporting mode, `0x13`/`0x1a`
19	IR-enable acks) and streams `0x30` core-button reports (~15 ms) for keep-alive.
20	On hardware: clean full handshake, the Wii assigns a player slot (`0x11`), and the
21	GPIO13 status LED (no real player LEDs on a Feather) goes **solid = assigned**
22	(heartbeat=waiting, fast-blink=connected). IR is acked but not implemented (only
23	needed for the pointer, not guitar gameplay).
24	
25	**Core-Wiimote + test-CLI workstream (before guitar).**
26	
27	- **Step A DONE — manual test CLI + connection management.** `esp_console` REPL
28	  (`console_cli.c`): `pair`/`stop`/`reconnect`/`unlink`/`status`/`btn`/`tap` — all
29	  thin pass-throughs over the module API (logic lives in `wiimote.c`/`bt_hid_device.c`,
30	  so Marvin can drive the same API later). Boots idle; `pair` arms the HID listeners
31	  for that sync window and `stop` tears them down; servers are **armed per pairing
32	  window**, not at boot or auto-re-armed (re-arming leaked L2CAP slots, since
33	  `reconnect` uses client connects). Honors the Wii's requested reporting mode
34	  (`0x12` → builds that report ID; buttons populated, accel/IR/ext zeroed). Disconnect
35	  fully resets state (`Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected`) and readers exit by L2CAP handle
36	  (robust to fd reuse). Bond persists in NVS (recalled at boot via
37	  `esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list`); `unlink` removes it. Status LED on GPIO13:
38	  blip/~3 s = idle, fast blink = pairing/connecting, N flashes = assigned player N.
39	- **Step B DONE — IR pointer.** Pointer `(x,y)` is a state variable in `wiimote.c`
40	  (`Wiimote_SetPointer`/`ClearPointer`), CLI `point x y` / `point off`. `build_ir_extended`
41	  synthesizes two sensor-bar dots into mode `0x33`'s 12-byte extended-IR field + a
42	  level accel. **Verified on hardware** — navigated the Wii menu and launched GH3 with
43	  it. Calibration constants (`IR_X/Y_CENTER/HALF`, from on-hardware edge measurement)
44	  map pointer 0..1 to the full screen, (0,0)=top-left. Basic-IR modes `0x36`/`0x37`
45	  are now filled too (`build_ir_basic` + shared `ir_dots`); the byte packing is
46	  verified against Dolphin's `IRBasic` struct and the Linux `hid-wiimote` decoder.
47	  Pointer tracks correctly on the main Wii screen and its Home overlay (basic `0x37`),
48	  so one calibration covers both modes (see the GH3-pointer note under Phase 3).
49	
50	**Phase 3 DONE — guitar extension plays GH3 (detection + frets + strum + whammy).**
51	On hardware: GH3 detects the guitar and frets/strum/whammy register in-game.
52	
53	- **Module split.** The guitar lives in its own `guitar.c` behind a small interface
54	  (`wiimote_ext.h`: `wiimote_extension_t` = register bank + `build_report`/`set_button`/
55	  `reset`; `Wiimote_RegisterExtension`). `wiimote.c` is now extension-agnostic (serves
56	  the registered bank for `0xa4xxxx` reg I/O, calls `build_report` for the ext field,
57	  delegates unknown button names to `set_button`). Buttons drive by name through
58	  `Wiimote_SetButton`/`TapButton` (green/red/yellow/blue/orange/strumup/strumdown/
59	  gplus/gminus/pedal); CLI `btn`/`tap`/`whammy`/`ext` are thin pass-throughs. Adding a
60	  nunchuk/classic later is just another self-registering `*.c`.
61	- **Report bit layout** (buttons **active-low**, rest = 1; verified against wiibrew +
62	  Linux `hid-wiimote`): byte0/1 = stick X/Y (bits5-0); **byte0/1 bits7-6 = 1 to
63	  identify a GH3 Les Paul** (0 = GHWT — with them clear GH3 treats us as GHWT and
64	  ignores the strum bar, which cost real debugging time); byte2 touchbar; byte3
65	  whammy; byte4 bit6 BD / bit4 B− / bit2 B+; byte5 bit7 BO / bit6 BR / bit5 BB /
66	  bit4 BG / bit3 BY / bit2 pedal / bit0 BU. GH3 streams mode **`0x37`** (not `0x34`);
67	  the ext field is filled for every ext-bearing mode (`0x32/34/35/36/37/3d`).
68	- **ENCRYPTION is required and now implemented** (`ext_crypto.c/.h`). GH3's actual
69	  handshake (from a register trace), *not* the old `0→0x40` init the plan guessed:
70	  `0x55`→`0xf0` (disable) → read ID at `0xfa` in the clear (decide GH3 vs GHWT) →
71	  `0xAA`→`0xf0` (re-enable) → 16-byte key to `0x40`-`0x4f`. Everything the game then
72	  reads (streamed ext bytes + the `0x20` calibration) is decrypted with that key, so
73	  plaintext reads as garbage. The base Wiimote captures the key, derives the ft/sb
74	  tables, and encrypts outgoing ext data (streamed bytes at reg offset `0x08`; reg
75	  reads at `addr & 7`); the guitar module stays plaintext. Cipher = the marcan Wii
76	  extension cipher; **rnconrad's `wm_crypto.c` tables are corrupted** (sbox[3]@0x60,
77	  [4]@0xd8, [6]@0x88/0xec — `0xD0`/`0xF0` & `0xD2`/`0xE2` flips, not valid
78	  permutations), so the tables were taken from **Dolphin's 1st-party** set and the
79	  algorithm verified term-for-term against Dolphin; round-trip validated against GH3's
80	  real key (idx 0 matched, encrypt→decrypt identity). Earlier "green/red work without
81	  encryption" was a decryption fluke.
82	- **Guitar-mode pointer (informational, not pursued).** Basic-IR pointer is correct on
83	  the main Wii screen + its Home overlay. *Inside GH3*, the Home-overlay cursor scales
84	  wrong — X over-sensitive, Y under, **opposite per axis** — which is GH3 applying its
85	  own pointer transform, not our IR (packing is verified identical to extended). Moot
86	  in practice: **with the Wiimote seated in the guitar the IR camera is physically
87	  blocked**, so guitar-mode Home nav uses the **analog stick (SX/SY)** instead. Kept a
88	  single IR calibration. Deferred idea: drive `SX/SY` (guitar module already owns them,
89	  fixed at center `0x20`) for guitar-mode Home navigation if Marvin ever needs it.
90	
91	**Link stability (done):** idle disconnects are fixed — Bluedroid's JV idle→sniff
92	delay (default 5 s) is overridden to 65 s via a `-D BTA_FTC_OPS_IDLE_TO_SNIFF_DELAY_MS`
93	in the top-level CMake (`#ifndef`'d `#define`; the timeout field is UINT16 + a 197 ms
94	offset, so stay < ~65338). With sniff effectively off the link stays active (Wii keeps
95	polling), so no supervision timeouts and no BTA PM-slot leak (the leak that previously
96	forced a power-cycle). **Auto-reconnect was removed** (2026-06-13): it didn't survive
97	the GH3 launch and is the wrong tool for keep-awake. Recovery from an unexpected drop
98	is now the explicit `reconnect` command; keep-awake is better served by occasional
99	input/state changes (which Marvin's command stream provides during use).
100	
101	**OPEN — GH3 game-launch handoff (needs a BT sniffer):** when a game disc boots, the
102	Wii goes HID-silent toward fauxmote for many seconds, then drops the link (`rsn 0x08`).
103	A manual `reconnect` re-establishes the link, but the session isn't reliably usable in-game.
104	A real Wiimote rides the handoff with a quick ~2 s LED off/on. fauxmote's own logs
105	don't show *why* the Wii goes silent on us vs a real Wiimote — there's no command we
106	visibly mishandle (zero RX reports during the gap). Diagnosing needs a Bluetooth
107	sniffer to diff a real Wiimote vs fauxmote through the GH3 launch. **Workaround for
108	now: restart fauxmote after the game has started** (a fresh boot reconnects cleanly).
109	The recurring `mode 3 … BASIC mode` reconnect warning is likely a red herring (real
110	Wiimotes use Basic-mode L2CAP for HID). Revisit after the guitar extension — GH3 may
111	engage the controller differently once it sees a guitar.
112	
113	**Other notes:**
114	- **Keep-awake:** the Wii idle-disconnects on lack of *input*; streaming reports +
115	  occasional button activity keeps it alive (free during gameplay).
116	- **Caveat:** a Wiimote cannot power a Wii on from standby (BT radio off); "wake" only
117	  means reconnecting while the console is already running.
118	
119	Phase progression and success criteria are in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) §6.

128	| 2026-06-13 | **Extension encryption is mandatory for GH3 and implemented in the base Wiimote (`ext_crypto.c`); the guitar module stays plaintext.** GH3's real key handshake (register trace): `0x55`→`0xf0` (disable) → read ID `0xfa` in clear → `0xAA`→`0xf0` (enable) → 16-byte key to `0x40`-`0x4f`. Dolphin is GPL and validated against real games; the marcan tables are reverse-engineered hardware constants (facts), reproduced with our own code. |
130	| 2026-06-13 | **Guitar is a self-registering extension module behind `wiimote_ext.h`; `wiimote.c` is extension-agnostic.** `wiimote_extension_t` = register bank + `build_report`/`set_button`/`reset`; `Wiimote_RegisterExtension`. Confirmed feasible building blocks in IDF v6.0.1: `SDP_CreateRecord`/`SDP_AddAttribute`/`SDP_AddSequence` (private `stack/sdp_api.h`) and `esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(psm)`. | Bluedroid is the only Classic-BT stack on ESP32, and its public APIs can't host an arbitrary SDP record (`esp_sdp` RAW is search-only). So the path requires *unsupported internals*: raise `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` via an injected `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN` compile define, build the exact Wiimote record with the internal SDP DB API, skip esp_hidd, and serve HID over raw L2CAP + hand-rolled HIDP. Wii BD_ADDR observed: `00:17:ab:07:2c:21`. | The Wii validates the SDP record against a real Wiimote's; esp_hidd's generic HID record (right VID/PID, wrong attributes + HID descriptor) fails the check, so it never proceeds to HID. Open: whether ESP-IDF lets us serve a fully custom SDP record (esp_sdp API vs internal Bluedroid `SDP_*` API) and listen on the fixed HID PSMs via `esp_bt_l2cap`. |
